rows.name: no-screen-key-bindings
rows.note: DK-16: the behavior is automatic for public controls, with ONE sanctioned seam — and the row's source scan is now a real one. WHAT IT PROVES: no module under src/controls names UserInputService, ContextActionService or Enum.KeyCode in CODE, and the lowercase binding sites are pinned exactly across THREE files — text_input.luau (2 — its text-entry Swallow and Cancel bindings, a control-owned sinking context, not a screen binding a key), row_actions.luau (4 — RowActionsDelete binds Delete+Backspace, RowActionsMenu binds ButtonX and Shift+Return; director-approved Tasks 8/8b, 2026-08-10), and menu.luau (3 — the platform-conventional menu keys Menu and Shift+F10 across three occurrence sites, shipped and gated in the navigation-and-menus round; pinned 2026-08-18 under release-candidate ruling R10, director veto open in the Step 13 report). Both are the SAME seam: contribution-scoped through bindActionSystem (the identical seam text_input.luau's own bindings ride), per-row focus-gated (ctx.setEnabled tracks `pathInsideRow`, never global), with the open menu owning ALL action dispatch while up (the MENU-OPEN CARVE-OUT guard on RowActionsDelete, review round 1 MAJOR) and the Shift+Return modifier match arbitrated through the identical priority/sink mechanism every other binding here already goes through — no second wiring path, so the raw UserInputService/ContextActionService/bare-Enum.KeyCode bypass class this check hunts does not apply. A THIRD file appearing, or either pinned count drifting, still reddens this check. The Studio fixture CREATES no binding either — the test is for a `keyCode =` assignment or a createAction/bind call, since the fixture READS `binding.keyCode` for its trace, which is observation, not wiring. The traversal case that proves the behavior presents with ZERO input opts. THREE DEFECTS THIS ROW HAS SURVIVED, each closed by making the INSTRUMENT better rather than the claim smaller. (1) CASE-BLINDNESS (phase-gate PG-2): the scans grepped `KeyCode` while the spelling at a binding site is lowercase `keyCode`, so a new control binding Tab was invisible — proven by copying stepper.luau to scratch, appending a bind, and watching every clause still pass; closed by pinning the lowercase sites. (2) LINE-COUNTING (2026-08-14): `grep -c` counts matching LINES, so the pin measured FORMATTING — round 3 consolidated row_actions' four key declarations into one `ROW_KEYS` table and the pin read 2 against 4, failing a refactor that removed nothing; the pins count OCCURRENCES, so a NEW binding still moves them. (3) COMMENT-BLINDNESS, twice: first a line comment naming `Enum.KeyCode` in row_actions' engineering rationale, patched with a grep filter for a `:<line>:<whitespace>--` line shape — which knows exactly ONE of Luau's four lexical forms. So when 3eb97fb added a `--[[ ]]` block comment to table.luau recording the live CAS-vs-InputContext measurement, the gate read two lines of prose as a binding, and this row plus traversal-document-order's `step8-debt-cleared` (which reads this gate's status out of gate.json) went RED. CLOSED 2026-08-15 by moving every source clause into `tools/check_no_screen_key_bindings.py`, whose stripper is a real lexer: long comments at ARBITRARY level (`--[==[ ]==]`), long strings, quoted and interpolated strings. String CONTENTS are deliberately left VISIBLE, because game:GetService(...) is the bypass being hunted and it lives inside a string. The allowlist was NOT widened and no clause was dropped. The row runs the script's own `--selftest` first (19 named lexer cases, themselves mutation-proved), and BOTH directions are proven at check level in a scratch copy of src/controls: a GetService bypass, an `Enum.KeyCode` use, a third binding file, a fifth `keyCode =` site and a fixture that wires input each redden it, while the same three tokens inside a NEW block comment do not. CEILING, stated so the next agent does not assume otherwise: a computed service name, a helper OUTSIDE src/controls binding on a control's behalf, and a changed KEY at an already-pinned site are all beyond any text scan — the script header names them and names the suite cases that cover the behavior instead.

rows.name: four-input-proofs
rows.note: PHASE-GATE FINDING C4, ACTED ON HERE RATHER THAN IN THE CHECKER, and the reasoning is the point. tools/lune/check_registration keys `inputProofs` on CONTROLS: it reads tests/conformance/controls_registry.luau, derives interactivity from a focusable leaf row or a `contribution.attach` in a composite's module, and demands all four classes. Round 2 added interactive behaviour that is NOT a control — `Table.onPrimaryAction` (a prop) and the playlist table's hosted `rowActions` (a prop) — so that checker passed while asserting nothing whatever about the new surface: green, and structurally unable to see the thing it should be checking. TWO THINGS WERE WRONG AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS THE CHECKER'S. (1) The proofs were unenforced. Fixed here, and fixed STRICTLY HARDER than mirroring the control path would have: check_registration's rule (b) is `string.find(source, caseName)` over the registered specs, which — by this manifest's own opening doctrine — proves a case is REGISTERED and never that it PASSES. These fourteen greps are anchored to `✓`, so they prove the proofs pass. Mirroring the control path would have imported a weaker assertion and called it enforcement. (2) COMPLETENESS — a FUTURE modifier or prop shipping interactive behaviour with no proofs at all — is NOT fixed, and is recorded as a named gap rather than papered over with machinery that cannot deliver it. A modifier has no mechanical interactivity signal to derive: `onPrimaryAction` is a blueprint prop with no `contribution.attach` of its own, so an automatic rule would have to heuristically scan prop schemas for names that smell interactive. That is precisely the noisy checker GameStudio/ENGINEERING.md's simplicity ladder says gets disabled, and it would buy nothing real — a hand-maintained registry of modifier rows only catches the next modifier if somebody remembers to add a row, which is the same `somebody remembers` that this gap already is. So: the obligation is enforced where it can bite, and the completeness hole is named. Both mouse orders are cited here because `after` bites through the tray and `before` through the selection, and citing only one of them would leave half the mouse claim unpinned again. rows.name: hosted-swipe-survives-release-activate
rows.note: REDTEAM NEW-1 (BLOCKER) AND NEW-2 (MEDIUM), 2026-08-13, and the pair is one check because it is one rule. A row `Hit` is a real engine `GuiButton`, so the pointer sequence that SWIPES it also ends in that button's own `Activated`, on either side of `InputEnded`. NEW-1: the hosted VirtualList armed its `suppressActivatePath` in exactly one place -- `onPointerUp`'s `unresolved` branch, a TAP on an already-open row -- so a gesture that resolved HORIZONTAL, i.e. every real swipe, armed nothing and the artifact fell straight into `spec.onActivate`. Measured through the real adapter seam on a clean-room hosted list: 8 of 12 combinations RED (both orders x both edges x both pointer kinds; only the four SILENT releases were green), where the Table twin this milestone already blocked on was merely order-dependent. On the shipped playlist analogue that reads `swipe to reveal Remove, and the track plays`. Fixed at `hostedResolveAxis` -- the one place this control decides a gesture went sideways -- exactly as `table.luau` arms at its own lock, and for the same reason: an `Activated` landing BEFORE `InputEnded` is already dispatched by the time any `onPointerUp` could arm anything. NEW-2: `a6229e0` cleared the arm only at the next pointer-DOWN, on the stated premise that `a real Activated always fires between a pointer-up and the next pointer-down`. THAT PREMISE IS FALSE for the two Activate producers that carry no pointer-down at all -- an IAS device Activate (`meta.source == "action"`), and the minimum-target hit expander, a SEPARATE `GuiButton` whose press produces no pointer event on the row's `Hit`. So a swipe ending with no `Activated` (a cancel, or an up off the translated hit) left the arm standing and ate the next device press: measured against 13fd3c6, `fired 0 -> 1` became `0 -> 0`, and a tray a device press used to close stayed open. Closed by clearing on CANCEL and by refusing to spend the arm on a device Activate at all, in BOTH controls. WHAT THIS CHECK PINS, and why each grep is here. The six matrix titles are the 12 combinations (each case drives BOTH edges on fresh worlds, because swiping the other way out of an open tray is the CLOSE gesture and would pass for the wrong reason); the two SILENT-release rows are the CONTROL that proves the matrix is not green merely because nothing activates. `the arm is one activate wide` is the counterweight that stops the NEW-2 clears from degenerating into `never arm`: the tap AFTER the swallowed artifact must still reach the control. The seven cancel/silent/device rows are NEW-2 on both surfaces -- including, on each, the MINIMUM-TARGET HIT EXPANDER, the second producer that carries no pointer-down and the one the `meta.source == "action"` half cannot cover (it is a POINTER Activate), so the CANCEL clear is proved load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces -- plus its own counterweight (`a swipe whose release DID Activate still swallows that artifact`) so `clear more often` cannot pass by never suppressing. EVERY ONE WAS MUTATION-PROVED TO REDDEN against the unfixed source, which is the only evidence that counts for two defects that hid behind checks structurally unable to fail: until `fake_target.pointerUpActivating` existed, every swipe case in this repo drove a release sequence the engine does not produce.

rows.note: ITEM D2, the director's request, and BOTH forms are pinned because shipping one of them would satisfy a looser check. DETERMINATE: `the SWEEP is the value: 25% ends at 3 o.clock, 100% closes the ring` is the arithmetic — an arc that merely appears is not a ring that FILLS to its value. INDETERMINATE: `the HEAD travels while the sweep stays fixed` is the design in one sentence (a fixed sweep whose START ANGLE advances), and it is the case that would fail if somebody re-implemented rotation on the presentation channel's `rotation` instead, which the mission deliberately did not use (it is presenter-owned and keyed by node path, so a control cannot reach it, and it is documented incompatible with ClipsDescendants). THE COST CLAIM IS ASSERTED, NOT ASSERTED-ABOUT: `a value change is PAINT ONLY: one prop write on .points., zero re-solves` and `60 frames of travel write points and never re-solve` are the whole reason this control could be built on Path2D at all — `points` is `dirty = { paint }`, and a regression that made the ring re-solve would be invisible to every geometry assertion while costing 600 solves over a 600-frame cycle (the measured indeterminate BAR does exactly that). OFF-PATH COST: `no circular indicator mounted = no Path instance and no .points. op, ever` is the brief's standing rule 3 obligation — prove the new feature's off-path cost is ~zero rather than asserting it — and mutation M14 (a stray UI.Path in the bar's builder) reddens it. REDUCED MOTION IS INHERITED, NOT RE-DECIDED: the ring reads the same phase value from the SAME single `informational` clock entry the dots read, so `takes the SAME single clock entry` pins that no second clock entry was acquired (which would have re-opened the scope/leak question) and `keeps advancing, on the quantized tick` pins the policy itself — a frozen spinner and a hung process look identical. THE FOUR GENERATED REFUSALS pin the capability registry that replaced three hand-written `if`s: a spinner with a value, `height` on a shape with no track, `showValue` on a shape with no room for it, and an unknown presentation listing the three that exist. `radius . size / 2 + thickness / 2 never exceeds size / 2` is the painted-at-a-size-nobody-measured family (a Path2D stroke is CENTRED on its curve) checked as arithmetic across the neutral snapshot and all eight shipped packages, because no headless diagnostic can see it. The two citations pin the SPLIT parity claim: the indeterminate ring is `ProgressView(.circular)` (SW-130) and the determinate one is a capacity gauge (SW-131), because the cited page says a circular progress view is not guaranteed to be determinate. The five clean-room proofs are the only artefacts in the repo written from a spec by an author who did not read framework internals, which is what makes them evidence rather than demos — so what is gated is the RE-PROOF's findings, not the diff. THE NINE CASES ARE THE SEVEN ADOPTIONS PLUS THE TRAP. Each is a DIFFERENCE assertion against what the previous code produced: the tag cloud was sixteen tags forced to an identical 135x23 by a uniform Grid and is now ragged on three lines; a post's two tags came out the same width as each other and now do not; five worn pieces each had their own line and now share one; `AT RAISED PREFERRED TEXT it REFLOWS to a second line instead of squeezing` is the strongest single proof in the set, because p4_foyer's deleted ladder carried the comment `reflow, never squeeze` — the definition of a flow wrap, written in prose by an author who had no word for it. THE TRAP IS WHY THREE OF THESE READ THE WAY THEY DO. The brief warned that `06_tile_game`'s ViewThatFits ladder wrote its readouts twice and moved them off their published paths past a green suite, because a LOSING candidate stays mounted with its props and text intact at a zero rect — so a presence assertion passes against content no player can see. p2_cartwheel was the same defect and worse (three published paths for `Charge`; the two losers measured 8x0 at EVERY viewport the section is reachable on). `each chip at ONE path, none at a zero rect` and `THE LADDER.S TWIN NODES ARE GONE` are therefore rect assertions, not presence assertions: they would both have passed with either ladder intact. `NOT ONE .Spacer. INSTANCE IS MOUNTED` is the same kind of claim from the instance side — `distribute` replacing hand-placed spacers is a stronger proof than adding a new call, because it shows the framework absorbed something the author previously had to hand-build (24 mounted Spacer instances to 0; 601 to 454 nodes at 1400x900). rows.name: audit-gaps-and-free-parity
rows.note: ITEM D — the ranked gaps taken (#12 onAppear/onDisappear, #16's hide), the ones deliberately left, and the free parity that was never claimed. THE TWO ORDERING DECISIONS ARE THE POINT OF THE FIRST FOUR GREPS. The cited pages decline to specify when these fire ([SW-138], [SW-139]), so Facet defined it: appear drains AFTER that frame's layout solve, so the callback can read its own rect (the earlier placement would have handed every hook a nil rect, which is the useless half of the capability), and disappear drains AFTER the removal sweep, so `rectOf(path)` is nil INSIDE the callback — asserted from in there, because that is the only place the ordering is observable. `does NOT fire again on a re-solve that changes no structure` is the negative control that stops `fire on every refresh` from satisfying the appear case. `surface teardown fires every still-mounted hook` is the leak direction chosen on purpose: a panel usually goes away by being dismissed, so a cleanup that only ran on re-keying would be a leak with a green suite. HIDDEN'S THREE CLAUSES, EACH SEPARATELY: it keeps its layout box (with `the whole difference from UI.When, whose sibling DOES move up` as the contrast that makes the claim non-vacuous), it leaves focus order, and it takes no tap. The last two exist because `paint` was the obvious dirty channel and was WRONG — a paint-only channel would have repainted the node and reached neither the focus-order filter nor the hit-rect retraction, shipping an invisible control that still takes Tab and still activates, which is half of that sentence sold as all of it. `...and so does a losing ViewThatFits candidate, which is the SAME verdict` pins that the gate reads the solver's MERGED hidden set rather than the authored prop alone — the case that caught a live Rascal Rally behaviour change within the hour (a spec driving `adapter.tap` into a 170x0 CTA in a losing candidate) and is the round-2 orchestration note one step worse: a test satisfied by a hidden copy, that DROVE the hidden copy. THE FREE PARITY: the four capabilities that already shipped and had never been rowed are pinned by name plus their citations, and the audit pointer keeps §13 pointing at the ranked list rather than at a silence a reader would fairly read as `considered and rejected`. SW-141/SW-142 are the two REFUSALS (`opacity`, `.disabled()` cascade) — a row that dropped them would let the next mission read either as an accidental omission rather than a recorded authority decision. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: the audit's other 36 capabilities are untouched and only enumerated; and neither capability has a Studio canary or a device run — in particular whether Roblox itself already refuses input to an invisible GuiButton is undocumented, which is exactly why the framework holds the rule rather than relying on the engine.

rows.name: chrome-four-inputs-and-settings
rows.note: ITEM E rows 4 and 11 — `[SHOWCASE-CHROME]: CONCERNS 16` executed, and the settings surface it hard-blocked. THE DEFECT WAS BIGGER THAN THE ROW SAID AND THE FIRST GREP IS THE HALF NOTHING HAD REPORTED: both pickers were `responder = passive`, a passive surface's nav context is created DISABLED, and the chrome re-presented itself after every demo mount — so the chrome's focus scope sat permanently on top and the DEMO was unreachable too. Driven headlessly before any change, Tab landed on a chip that paints no ring and Return/ButtonA no-opped against the demo's handle. `Tab reaches the demo, not the chip strip` is that regression, and it is first because a fix that only made the chrome reachable would have left it standing. THE FOUR-INPUT PROOF IS DRIVEN THROUGH THE DEVICE SEAM, never through an API: `system.deviceKey` through the real InputBinding table and `adapter.tap` through the real hit path. The gamepad leg runs with `capabilities.keyboard = false` so no keyboard binding can be helping it — that is what makes `with no keyboard anywhere` an assertion rather than a title. THE TWO COUNTERWEIGHTS ARE WHY THE RESTRUCTURE IS TWO SURFACES AND NOT ONE `engage()` CALL: `one Tab press moves the ring one step, not two` fails the moment the strip engages alongside the panel (two engaged surfaces both sit at the engaged band's 3000 and both receive Traverse), and `binds exactly the two documented keys, and nothing a demo uses` is asserted by pressing all twelve contended keys and requiring that none of them toggles the chrome — Backquote and ButtonY were chosen precisely because every other candidate is claimed (Escape is engine-reserved, Tab is Traverse and CoreGui-contended, ButtonA is eaten by the legacy jumpAction, ButtonB is Cancel, ButtonX is the row-actions menu). THE LADDER: `steps down to icons rather than clipping` is CONCERNS 16's arithmetic executed, and `the losing rung is out of the focus order at every width` is the hidden-candidate class asserted on the chrome's own ladder. THE SETTING IS A SETTING AND NOT A DEMO'S SIDE EFFECT: `flipping it RE-SOLVES without rebuilding` proves round 2's reason 3 rather than restating it (factory runs and instance count unchanged while `motionClock:isReduced()` goes true — mutation M15 makes the write a no-op and it reddens), and `the host.s re-apply is what makes the SETTING win over that restore` is the exact sequence that separates the place-wide preference from a demo's documented restore-on-dispose. `no player-visible string says on, off, disable or enable` enforces the Full|Reduced vocabulary decision — the env fact is binary but the effect is not. THE SHOWCASE RULE IN FULL: the chrome is NOT reachable by tests/overflow_sweep.spec.luau, so it sweeps itself — both surfaces, both sections, eight viewports, eight shipped packages, failing on either axis (128 mounts), plus the 320x640 non-overlap case and a ~1.4x pseudo-localization pass. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: no Studio canary was run. Whether a real Backquote reaches IAS and whether a physical ButtonY fires Activate end to end are both open — injected keys are known-unreliable for some classes and a pad button cannot be pressed headlessly. RE-PINNED 2026-08-22 under RULING R20 (2026-08-21), which took `ButtonY` off this chrome because it is `menu.luau`'s gamepad menu verb. `the pad.s toggle button opens the panel` became `the pad.s shoulder opens the panel` — the same claim (a pad-only capability set opens, engages and lands focus inside the panel) on `SECTION_GAMEPAD.demos`, which is the route the chips now advertise with a glyph. `binds exactly the two documented keys` became `three` — one keyboard toggle plus two pad section doors — and it got STRONGER, because `ButtonY` MOVED INTO the contended set the case sweeps: the row now also proves the chrome does not steal the framework's menu verb.

rows.name: large-text-sweep-axis
rows.note: THE ALWAYS-ON SWEEP GAINED TWO AXES THIS ROUND and both are pinned here, because a sweep is an instrument and an instrument that stops asking a question does so silently. The CROSS axis came from item A (a wrapping stack cannot overflow its main axis — that is what wrapping means — so a wrapping stack on any screen would have been structurally invisible to a sweep that greps `on the main axis`), and the TEXT-SIZE axis came from the same blind spot biting twice in one sitting: the perf lab's rows overflowed by 11/39/59px at preferredTextOffset 4/10/14 and were clean at 0, and p4_foyer's TopBar was pre-existing and invisible for exactly the same reason. THE TWO CONTROL CASES ARE THE ONLY THING THAT KEEPS THIS HONEST, and they are why this row is not a `check that proves nothing`: `AXIS CONTROL` mounts a slot sized for Larger and asserts SILENCE at +0/+4/+10 and a REPORT at +14 including the exact 6px, so if the axis is ever disabled that case says so on that run; and `every waived large-text overflow still fires` is the waiver machinery's own tripwire — a waiver is a CEILING and not a pardon (a finding that exceeds it, or appears at a SMALLER preference, fails) and a waiver that fires nowhere fails too, so the enumerated list of 35 known defects can only shrink. Nothing is waived at offset 0, so the pre-axis contract is untouched. THE THREE NAMED SCENARIOS are round 2's three, re-pinned at their CURRENT case titles — the sweep is parameterised over a registry, so naming them makes a scenario's disappearance a gate failure rather than a smaller green run, and the rename is recorded in the round-2 block above because that block's own greps were left pointing at the old titles and were RED at the moment round 3 was registered. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: the sweep still runs ONE LOCALE (measured stronger than this axis on at least one surface), 390x844 is still not a swept viewport, and the sweep still cannot see the `virtualSlot` finding's phrase — all three are booked in artifacts/swiftui-parity-round3/owed.md rather than papered over.

rows.name: virtual-slot-guard
rows.note: THE LYING `itemExtent` GUARD (director-approved 2026-08-13). `newVirtualList` windows by `index x itemExtent`, which is O(1) and exact ONLY because the extent is one declared number — and the control makes the CONSUMER predict its own row's height for every live fact the cell reads. Nothing checked the prediction, and the case study is the perf lab's `heightFor`, whose comments record it learning viewport width, then the type scale (3px), then theme insets (19px), then — found on a real device — the accessibility text preference (11/39/59px): four inputs, three of them added post-mortem. FOUR OF THESE NINE GREPS ARE SILENCE CASES, and that ratio is the design: a diagnostic that fires on honest rows gets disabled, which is worse than not shipping it. Legitimately-short rows say nothing (over-reservation is the correct direction), a cell that ABSORBS its own overflow says nothing (the exception zstack_fill_diagnostic.spec was written for), a hidden subtree says nothing, and the control's OWN full-row hit Button is excluded via `contentFrom` — without which every list denser than 24px would be accused of a lie the framework itself wrote. THE FIRE CASES pin that it names BOTH numbers (the declared extent and the measure, so the finding is actionable rather than an accusation) and that it tracks the preference (4 -> 60, 14 -> 84). `SEES a cell that declares height = fill` is the one place in solver.luau that does not excuse a fill axis, and it is load-bearing: 254 of 791 positive deltas across the suite sit on a fill main axis, shapes the previous ZStack overlap finding was structurally blind to. `compares against the DECLARED extent, never the row.s current box` is the case that keeps a hosted row-actions commit collapse — which drives one row's box down its own height ladder on purpose — from making the guard shout. THE ALWAYS-ON SWEEP CAN NOW SEE THIS CLASS, and the last grep is where that is pinned: when this row was first written the sweep greped two axis phrases and this finding says `than the slot it is windowed into`, so the class was enforced only by the perf lab's mount check, Rascal Rally's large-text fixtures and this spec. rows.name: solve-count-coalescing
rows.note: L-27's LEVER, PAID. The device capture produced a ranked list and the top item was not a slow function, it was a COUNT: `arrange` 8.270 ms/occurrence and 9.67 arranges per step on a physical device, against L-27's standing record that one viewport change costs 5 solves — roughly 45 ms of a ~200 ms frame. THE INVESTIGATION IS WHY THE FIRST CASE READS THE WAY IT DOES: a bare `env:set(viewportRect, ...)` on a mounted 40-row tree cost exactly ONE solve at every size, so the defect would not reproduce headless at all. The seam headless does not have is the ADAPTER — `roblox_env.pushViewport()` writes SIX facts on one real resize — and mimicking exactly those six writes reproduced L-27's 5 on the first try. Two multipliers were compounding and NEITHER FIX WORKS ALONE (batching alone: 5; coalescing the eight independent geometry-key observers alone: 4; both: 1), which is why `a batched geometry change is ONE solve` is the case and not `fewer solves`. `every geometry key still re-solves` is its negative control — a memo that coalesced by never recomputing would satisfy the first case perfectly and break the framework — and `a non-geometry write does not solve` bounds the memo's dependency set from the other side. `env:batch is the general mechanism` pins standing rule 2: this is `core:transaction` exposed on the environment and applied to the adapter's three fact-groups, not a viewport special case. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: the device number itself. It is a headless solve-COUNT contract, which is the portable half of a tier-3 finding; the ms are tier 3 and not re-measurable here. Two open items ride with it and are booked rather than hidden: a presented modal still costs 2 solves per geometry change (L-29 residual 2, with the consumer rider asserting a CEILING of 2 so the second solve can be removed later without moving the check), and the lab overlay's measure-then-publish feedback loop.

rows.name: popup-catcher-paint
rows.note: THE POPUP CATCHER DECLARED NO SURFACE, SO EVERY THEME PAINTED IT (fix commit 7fb325f). A dismiss catcher is a hit region, not a plate — but it went out with no surface declaration, so a theme package with a default plate painted one over the viewport, visible in practice only in the band the owner's own DisplayOrder did not cover. THE THREE GREPS ARE THE DEFECT, ITS SIBLING AND ITS EXPLANATION, and the second is the one that makes this more than a spot fix: the catcher is reached through TWO `outsideDismiss` owners, and fixing the path the report named while leaving the sibling caller broken is the failure mode ENGINEERING.md's `grep every caller` rule exists for. The third pins the DisplayOrder relationship that explains why the bug was nearly invisible — which is worth pinning precisely because a future change that raised the catcher's band would make the same latent paint fully visible. rows.note: HALF RUN 2026-08-14, AND THE HALF THAT DID NOT RUN IS WHY THIS ROW IS STILL NOT A PASS. Round 3 shipped four surfaces whose remaining questions only a live session can answer, and every one of them closed headless-green with an explicit rider in the mission record. TWO ARE NOW ANSWERED, in a live Studio EDIT datamodel against the real screen_target adapter (the evidence file above; tier 2, never a device claim). ITEM A — the `flow_wrap` fixture had never been mounted in an engine at all; it is mounted now, and its own A/B was driven at 389x762: wrapped, the fourteen tags occupy FOUR lines and diagnostics is empty; unwrapped, one line reaching x=1183 and the solver reports `content overflows this hstack by 806px on the main axis`. The captures also say something the numbers do not — only five tags PAINT, because the page's own ScrollView crops the rest, so the diagnostic's `it will paint outside its box` is the honest worst case rather than what a player sees. ITEM D2 — BOTH halves answered, and both flip an assumption. (a) `ClipsDescendants` does NOT crop a Path2D stroke: the same octagon drawn in a clipping and a non-clipping 200x200 panel paints identically past the edge in both, while GetBoundingRect returns 147x147 for both — so a `presentation = "circular"` ring inside a scrolling or clipping host paints outside it and no diagnostic can see it, which is a live-only defect class. (b) `Path2D:UpdateControlPoint` — the cheap in-place mitigation — SUCCEEDS on a parented Path2D and refuses only on an unparented one (`Attempting to use Path2D with invalid parent`); the framework always parents its Path2D under a holder Frame, so that path is open. The arc's cost was measured in writes rather than guessed: 121 -> 9,169 propWrites across 120 heartbeats, ~75 per frame, on DESKTOP Studio — a magnitude for a phone number to be compared against, not a phone budget. STILL NOT RUN, and this is the blocker rather than an excuse: the Studio MCP Play bridge is unavailable in this environment — start_stop_play times out and then answers `Start play hasn't finished yet` for the rest of that instance's life, and while a session IS in Play, execute_luau answers `Target is not reachable` for BOTH the Client and Server datamodel; reproduced on two Studio instances, the second fresh. Synthetic CGEvent clicks and System Events keystrokes do not reach Studio either (proved against an Explorer row and a ribbon tab). So ITEM D — whether Roblox itself already refuses input to an invisible GuiButton — stays unanswered for want of delivered input, though the canary did record the shipped shape behind it (every `hud` node outside the viewport box is a `FacetHitExpander`: a TextButton, Visible = true, BackgroundTransparency = 1, painting nothing). ITEM E — a real Backquote reaching IAS, and a physical ButtonY firing Activate end to end — needs Play and hardware and stays PENDING_PHYSICAL. So does everything presenter-shaped: `roblox_input.newSystem` requires Players.LocalPlayer, which an Edit datamodel does not have, so there is no presenter and no InputContext in this canary at all. SPELLED AS FAIL_ENVIRONMENT WITH releaseBlocking = false, which is this manifest's established shape for work that is blocked on hardware or a human session (every PENDING_PHYSICAL row in every stage above): it reads as a non-PASS in the roll-up and in gate.json, it is visible to anyone reading the gate, and it does not block the phase — while a bare PENDING would make the gate structurally un-passable and would therefore be deleted rather than closed. IT KEEPS THAT SPELLING even though two of its four questions closed, because the row is the SESSION, not the question list: the four questions are enumerated individually in artifacts/swiftui-parity-round3/owed.md, which still carries O-3 as PENDING_PHYSICAL, and a row that went green on the Edit-datamodel half would retire the Play half with it.

rows.name: time-based-easing
rows.note: ADR-0033. THE FOUR ADR GREPS AT THE END ARE THE POINT OF THIS ROW, and they are pinned as WITHDRAWALS rather than as claims, because this decision is the one place in round 4 where the mission argued itself out of two of its own headlines and a future editor tidying struck-through prose would silently restore both. WITHDRAWAL 1 — the consumer proof. The ADR originally cited RascalRally's `CommitBeatModel` `p^1.6` ease-in as a curve the Facet port `had to flatten to a linear clock:timer`. The rider it commissioned falsified it: 1.6 shapes a blink FREQUENCY ramp (integrated closed-form), which no value-at-time curve can express at all; only the legacy modules call it; the blink was removed by director amendment A24; and legacy's own visible swell is linear, so the port is a faithful match. `No shipped consumer had a curve taken away from it.` is the surviving sentence and it is pinned. WITHDRAWAL 2 — `native is the default`. Pinned by `AMENDED 2026-08-15.` and by `RascalRally requires motion_driver nowhere`. WHAT THIS ROW THEREFORE REFUSES TO SAY: that the shipped consumer gets engine easing. It does not. All four of Rascal Rally's Facet surfaces hand-roll their frame source and none binds `motion_driver`, so on the one live consumer every curve evaluates on the PURE TWIN. WHAT IT ALSO REFUSES TO SAY, and this is the opposite error: that the engine evaluator is absent. It is not — `TweenService:GetValue` IS the production evaluator, installed onto the clock by `motion_driver.bind`, and `routes every evaluation through the installed evaluator` is the case that proves the seam is live. The amended claim was about the BIND being universal, never about the evaluator existing. AND IT IS NOT A SPEED CLAIM: `The engine is not cheaper here.` plus the literal `58.6 ns` pin the measurement that makes the choice honest — 58.6 ns per engine call against 9.2 ns of pure Lua, SIX POINT THREE TIMES SLOWER, adopted anyway because it is canonical. A gate that let `native` quietly come to mean `faster` would be re-telling the exact story the ADR refuses to tell. THE ORACLE IS A RECORDED SESSION, NOT A HEADLESS COMPARISON, and the row is built so it cannot pretend otherwise: `matches the frozen engine corpus at every sampled alpha` names a FROZEN corpus because Lune never calls TweenService — the live 33,033-sample differential run (11 styles x 3 directions x 1,001 alphas, max |twin - engine| 4.73e-7) lives in artifacts/time-based-easing/engine-oracle.md and the suite compares against 50 samples captured from it. The oracle earned its keep: the twin first shipped with Penner's p = 0.3 and was off by 0.0248 on elastic in all three directions until it was refit to the engine's p = 1/3.25. THE DURATION IS THE FEATURE: `ARRIVES EXACTLY ON TIME, and not one frame early` and `advances by RAW dt` are the two halves of the thing no spring can promise. THE REGISTRY SHIPS EMPTY and refuses an inline spec, which is the same drift rule the spring classes already carry. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: any per-frame device cost (the ns figures are Studio, tier 2), and it does NOT cite tools/lune/oracle_easing.luau, which src/motion/curves.luau's header used to name and which has never existed — the header was corrected in wave R5 to cite the artifact, which is the oracle.

rows.name: foreign-instance-seam
rows.note: ADR-0034, AND THE SEAM IS INVERTED — that inversion is the whole decision and it is pinned from both sides. The comparison document that commissioned this ranked it as React-Lua's escape hatch and sketched a `contentRoot()` that hands the caller a Facet-owned Instance. The ADR refuses that shape and says so in the heading itself (`the seam hands back nothing`), with `This departs from the shape` marking it as a deliberate departure rather than an oversight. What ships is `controller.foreignHost(path)` answering ONE verb, `adopt(instance)`: the caller passes THEIR instance IN, and nothing Facet owns travels OUT. That literal sentence is pinned because it is the sentence that keeps `Ref` deferred — the authority argument that defers handing out a framework-owned instance is untouched by a seam that never hands one out, and `stays deferred` pins that consequence in place. `retains no reference to the adopted content, so it cannot write to it later` is the structural half of the same claim, and it is the case that separates this from a promise: `is structural, not a promise` in the ADR, a registry assertion in the suite. THE RESERVED `host` AUTHORITY WENT LIVE HERE, which is the second half of the row. `host` sat declared and unused in src/render/authority.luau since the authority manifest was written, with a header claiming it was reserved for exactly this; ADR-0034 spent it, and the row pins that it owns EXACTLY ONE property (`Foreign.Parent`), that it is the manifest.s only `host` entry, and that the second-writer gate catches a rival for it. `claims NOTHING else: every other Foreign prop resolves through common` is the negative control without which `owns exactly one property` could be satisfied by an authority that quietly owned several. THE FIVE REFUSALS, each separately, because each is a different way to widen the hatch by accident: the UNBOUNDED form (a `UI.Native{class=}` that would make every Roblox class reachable) is refused BY NAME with the argument and the alternative; `tint` is refused because Facet never paints the caller.s content; and `adopt` refuses nothing, a LayerCollector, a non-GuiObject and a destroyed instance, each named. rows.name: preferred-transparency
rows.note: ADR-0035, AND THE SCOPE IS A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN A TASTE CALL — which is what makes this gateable at all. Roblox's PreferredTransparency is a player accessibility setting, and the tempting implementation is a sweep over everything that looks see-through. The ADR refuses that and instead pins the scope to a MEASURED fact: of the generated sheet.s eight surface branches exactly one, the scrim backdrop, writes a BackgroundTransparency strictly between 0 and 1. `the ONLY rule painting a see-through background is the backdrop` asserts that measurement, and `the declared patch scope is exactly the measured set of translucent backgrounds` is the equality that makes it load-bearing rather than decorative: it is a SET EQUALITY, so the row reddens both when the patch scope grows (a shadow or a hairline joining it) and when the sheet grows a second translucent background nobody added to the scope. The compiled-package twin beside it is there because a floor only one builder emits vanishes the moment a player picks a theme package. THE REFUSALS ARE PINNED HONESTLY AND UNEVENLY, and the unevenness is stated rather than hidden. TWO have named cases: the disabled dim (`the alpha there is the state, not a backdrop`) and the hairline (`a stroke is a border, and the setting names backgrounds`). THE SHADOW AND FOCUS-GLOW REFUSALS HAVE NO CASE OF THEIR OWN — grep the spec for `shadow` or `glow` and there is nothing — so they are pinned where they actually live, as the ADR sentence `A shadow that is opaque is a black box, and a glow that is opaque is a rectangle.`, plus the set-equality case above, which is what would redden if either joined the scope. Writing a suite grep for a shadow case name would have been a pattern that can never match, and that is a check that cannot fail in the worst direction: silently. `scaling an INVISIBLE background does not dim it, it reveals it` is the argument for the whole refusal family in one case — 0 is unchanged by any multiply and 1 would be REVEALED by one, so the naive sweep does not merely overreach, it inverts. THE AUTHORED CHANNEL IS SEPARATE AND STAYS SEPARATE: `opacity 0.5 stays 0.5 at every preference` is decision 2 executed, and it is the case that fails if the preference is ever folded into presentation.composeAlpha where it would multiply an author.s number and a withAnimation term. THE FRAMEWORK PUSHES, THE CONSUMER WIRES NOTHING: attach plus mid-session plus a clamp on garbage, all three, because a push that only happened at attach would look identical in every static assertion. TWO WRITERS, ONE COMPOSITION: the bespoke painter and the native rule patch are asserted separately to go through `backdropTransparency`, which is a source contract rather than a behaviour — both live in modules that reach engine globals at load and cannot be behaviourally mutated under Lune. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: the live numbers. artifacts/adr-0035-preferred-transparency/live-probes.md carries the GetStyled readings from a real session; nothing here re-measures them.

rows.name: sorted-entries-determinism
rows.note: `UI.sortedEntries`, AND THE ONLY THING WORTH GATING ABOUT IT IS THAT ITS DETERMINISM TEST CAN ACTUALLY FAIL. The feature is four lines of sort; the hazard is that the obvious test for it is inert. `pairs` over a Lua table is not random — it is a deterministic function of the table.s internal hash layout — so `flatten the same dictionary twice and compare` PASSES with the sort REMOVED, every time, on every run. The axis that moves is CONSTRUCTION HISTORY, not repetition: the same twelve key/value pairs inserted ascending, descending, shuffled, and churned (twelve real keys plus twelve ghosts, ghosts then deleted) lay out differently and iterate differently. THE SPEC SHIPS THE INERT CHECK ON PURPOSE, AS A NAMED CASE (`the naive determinism check would PASS with pairs — repetition is the wrong axis`), so the trap is documented in the one place a future author is guaranteed to read. `THE NEGATIVE CONTROL — the same twelve pairs iterate in DIFFERENT orders` is the case that makes every other case in the file meaningful: it asserts the raw orders are FOUR distinct strings, so if a Luau change ever made `pairs` insertion-ordered the whole file would announce that its premise had evaporated instead of passing vacuously. AND SIX KEYS PROVES NOTHING: `at SIX keys three of the four constructions agree — which is why this file uses twelve` is that fact measured and kept as a case, because twelve is not an arbitrary fixture size and a later author trimming it to six would silently re-inert the whole spec. THE GUARANTEE ITSELF is `ORDERS KEYS, NOT ENTRIES` — pinned in source and asserted as `the comparator receives KEYS, which is what makes the guarantee unconditional`. That is not a stylistic choice: keys are unique, so any strict order over them is a TOTAL order and ties are impossible, whereas a comparator over ENTRIES can tie on equal values and hand the sort back its input order, which is the nondeterminism the helper exists to remove, restored through the front door. The refusal beside it (a key type with no natural order is refused AT CONSTRUCTION, naming the comparator) is the same rule enforced rather than documented. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: anything about `table.sort` stability, which Luau does not promise and which the KEYS rule makes irrelevant.

rows.name: two-dimensional-focus
rows.note: ADR-0030. THE DECISION IS AN AXIS PAIR, NOT A NEW GROUP KIND: a `columns` integer on the NavigationGroup that already exists, so the lane direction stays whatever `axis` said and the perpendicular direction moves plus or minus `columns`. `adds no ordering opinion at all` is pinned because that is the property that made this cheap — the group.s order is still the order its owner declared, and `columns` only says how to read it. THE STRONGEST CASE IN THIS ROW IS THE NULL HYPOTHESIS: `1-D groups walk byte-identically with the field absent`. Every 2-D path is gated on `columns` being a usable integer, so a group that declares none navigates through the same code as the graph that never heard of a second axis; without that case the whole feature could have regressed every existing focus group and the geometry assertions would not have noticed. THE RAGGED-LINE PAIR IS THE ARITHMETIC MOST LIKELY TO BE GOT WRONG and is pinned in both directions with its own negative control: FORWARD clamps into a short last line rather than falling out of the group, and `clamping is NOT a wrap: from the last line itself the move exits` is what stops `clamp` from quietly becoming `wrap`. `wrap governs the group.s DECLARED axis only; the perpendicular exits` and `exiting perpendicular hands the LANE on, so the column survives the crossing` pin the two rules that decide what a grid feels like at its edges. THE ORACLE ROW IS DIFFERENTIAL AND IT BITES: the ring is checked against an independent (line, lane) coordinate model over 300 seeded grids and walks, and `THE CORPUS BITES: the oracle rejects a one-cell perpendicular step` is the control proving the corpus can fail — a generated corpus that agrees with everything is a random number generator with a green tick. BOTH INTERCEPTS ARE GONE, AND THIS IS PINNED AS A REPLACEMENT RATHER THAN AN ABSENCE. src/controls/virtual_grid.luau (ONE control, parameterised, serving both vertical grid and sideways grid) used to carry a hand-written `navigateIntercept` that caught the perpendicular key, computed index plus or minus lanes, scrolled, and called focusOn, plus a `bindFocusGraph` to get the graph in the first place. Both are deleted and `columns = lanesNow()` on the contributed group replaces them. The row asserts `bindFocusGraph` is ABSENT from that file outright and that the file still carries its own `THERE IS NO ...` deletion note — a plain absence grep is NOT usable here, because the word `navigateIntercept` legitimately survives four times in the comments that explain the deletion, and a naive `! grep -q navigateIntercept` would be red today and for the wrong reason. The VirtualGrid and VirtualHGrid keyboard cases are the acceptance test: they were NOT modified by the change, so a grid that still moves a whole line on Down through a completely different mechanism is the proof the intercepts were redundant rather than load-bearing. THE STANDING-RULE-4 GAP, RECORDED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: THIS CLOSURE SHIPPED NO SHOWCASE FIXTURE. `git show 4ba1a6d` touches zero files under examples/, demo_picker.DEMOS has no 2-D-focus entry among its 32, and no scenario was added — the two grid demos it was exercised against (`virtual-grid`, `virtual-hgrid`) predate it and their blurbs still describe the intercept era. Its two sibling closures in the same sitting DID get fixtures (branch_scope and sorted_entries, both in d73404b), which is what makes this an omission rather than a policy. It is left open deliberately: building a fixture inside a gate-registration task would be the gate author writing the product work he is about to grade, and the honest record is worth more here than a demo written to satisfy a row. The live evidence that does exist is artifacts/two-dimensional-focus/live-studio.md, a Studio session driving the two pre-existing demos. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: no device run, no fixture, and nothing about `emitGridGroups`, which the ADR explicitly declines to convert.

rows.name: tint-fill-tag
rows.note: A TINTED BOX PAINTED NOTHING, AND THE REASON IS THE ROW.S WHOLE SUBJECT: A DEFAULT-VALUED WRITE CLAIMS NOTHING. Under native stylesheets the engine decides whether a property is explicitly set by comparing it to the class default, not by remembering that somebody assigned it. A tint whose transparency is the default 0 wrote 0 onto a Frame whose BackgroundTransparency default IS 0, so the write claimed nothing, the sheet.s `Frame default` rule (= 1) kept ownership, and every plate came out fully transparent. The colour half was fine — a real non-default colour is a real claim — which is why the bug looked like the tint was ignored rather than half-applied. THE FIX IS A CASCADE POSITION, NOT A WRITE: the fill moved onto a `facet-tint-fill` TAG whose rule sits after `Frame default` and before `Base surface`, `Control fill` and the scrim, so it wins the default and loses to everything a surface actually declares. `emits the tint fill in the same cascade position as the legacy builder` is the package half, and it is not optional: a floor only one builder emits vanishes the moment a player picks a theme package, which is the RS-A16-D4 class this codebase already paid for once. THIS ROW MAKES A SMALLER CLAIM THAN ITS NAME SUGGESTS, AND THE GAP IS THE INTERESTING PART. NO TEST IN THIS REPOSITORY PROVES A TINTED BOX PAINTS. The test lib mirrors the pure resolvers and models no StyleSheet cascade and no GetStyled at all, so a fake adapter models the WRITE and not the engine.s refusal of it. Two green cases were green throughout the entire period the feature painted nothing, and one of them is titled `every tile paints a REAL tint — the plate is never invisible` while asserting `tintTransparency == 0`, which is exactly the value that claimed nothing: a false witness for painting, deliberately NOT greped here. What this row pins instead is everything that IS assertable headlessly: the tag exists and is emitted by both builders at the same cascade position; the adapter sets and clears `tintFill` and re-syncs its tags (a source contract, because screen_paint reaches engine globals at load); a DECLARED transparency of 0.35 still resolves to 0.35 through the claim path; and the theme-repaint cases pin that a re-solve now REPAINTS a static tint, which it did not before `9b79333`. THE PAINT PROOF ITSELF IS THE LESSON DOCUMENT, and it is pinned as evidence rather than dressed up as a test: GetStyled is the only instrument that can see any of this, and the live reading (raw 0 / GetStyled 1 before, GetStyled 0.000 on all six plates after, .facet-tint-fill in the live sheet at priority 70, 16 of 16 tint-fill nodes painted on the virtual-grid demo) exists only in that session and in docs/lessons/a-default-valued-write-never-claims.md. If the framework ever grows a cascade simulator, this row should gain a real painted assertion and lose this paragraph.

rows.name: zstack-hugging-margin
rows.note: A SOLVER BUG THAT SURVIVED BECAUSE THE ONE ALIGNMENT EVERYONE USES AGREES WITH IT. In the `zstack` arm of `arrange`, a HUGGING child had its margins subtracted from the offer it was measured against and was then ALIGNED IN THE BOX IT HAD BEEN DENIED. `start` gives the same answer either way, which is why nine years of start-aligned overlays never noticed; `end` put the far edge flat on the stack.s inner edge, so a trailing margin bought nothing at all, and `center` centred in the full box and then displaced the child by the leading margin. THE FIVE LAYOUT CASES ARE THE ALIGNMENT TRUTH TABLE, WHICH IS THE ONLY SHAPE THAT COULD HAVE CAUGHT THIS: end on both axes, near margin, centre, and `a START-aligned child is unmoved` as the negative control that pins the population that was always correct — without it a fix could have moved everything and passed. `a CENTRED child centres in the box it was GIVEN, not the box it was denied` is the root cause stated as arithmetic a mutation cannot satisfy by accident. THE SYMPTOM IS PINNED SEPARATELY BECAUSE IT IS WHAT A PLAYER SAW: the Table header.s sort mark painted ON the theme plate.s carved border, outside its own box, under every package that carves contentInsets. `the mark clears the plate.s carved border, so it paints INSIDE the box` and `no package makes the header band report a layout finding` run that across the whole shipped package set, which is the corpus the lesson says did not previously exist — `A corpus uniform along an axis cannot test that axis` is pinned because the neutral theme carves nothing, so every existing header test was blind to this by construction. THE TWO RESERVATION FOLLOW-ONS ride here rather than in a row of their own: the header title now reserves BOTH terms of the mark (margin plus text size) and pays for it on a LEADING title too, which is the sibling caller the original reserve missed. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: nothing was captured in Studio for the fixed header — the nine-package sweep is headless, and the carved-border geometry is asserted against solved rects, not against pixels.

rows.name: native-scroll-autobind
rows.note: O-31, CLOSED BY CONTRADICTING ITS OWN ROW — and rowed HERE because round 3 asserts only that three files exist. The round-3 owed-ledger row does `test -f` on src/controls/native_scroll_binding.luau, tests/native_scroll_autobind.spec.luau and the artifact, and greps none of their content: all three could be emptied to stubs and that gate stays green. This row is the behaviour. THE DEFECT: a virtualised collection windows on its own scroll offset, and an ENGINE scroll (a real finger on a real ScrollingFrame moving CanvasPosition) was not mirrored back unless the consumer remembered to call `bindNativeScroll(controller)` after `present`. Measured live, an engine scroll to y=2000 left a 5,000-cell grid still showing c1..c16. Five of nine callers omitted the call. THE LEDGER NAMED THE WRONG SEAM AND THE FIX PROVED IT WRONG BY MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN BY ARGUMENT, which is why `PROOF THE DISCRIMINATOR IS REAL` is a case and not a comment: the row proposed delivering the controller through `buildFocusGroups`, described as the one seam that hands a control its mounted path. It is not, and it does not reach — the presenter calls a contribution.s `focusGroups` ONLY from `focus_map.autoGroups`, which runs only when the consumer left `navigationGroups` ABSENT. Across four presenter configurations `focusGroups` fires 2, 0, 0, 0 while `bindController` fires 1, 1, 1, 1. So the ledger.s own fix would have repaired the default screen and left every consumer that declares a focus map exactly as broken, and the three `...and it still does when the CONSUMER declares navigationGroups` cases are that finding turned into a guard. THE FOUR CONTROLS ARE PINNED SEPARATELY (list, both grid axes, table) because they are three different hosts sharing one arbitration module and the axis pair is where a transpose bug would hide. IDEMPOTENCE AND UNBIND STICKINESS are the compatibility story for Rascal Rally.s hand-rolled bind, which still exists and must not double-observe. THE OPT-OUT IS A PUBLISHED FACT, NOT A FOURTH SPEC KEY: `a BLOCK table (scrolls = false) auto-binds NOTHING — its published scroll path is nil`, and api.md.s `There is no opt-out key` sentence is pinned so the next mission does not add one. `NEGATIVE CONTROL: a bare mount with no presenter still learns no path, and says so` bounds the feature from the other side. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: src/present/ was not touched and the row.s named scope stays an over-estimate on the record; and the live A/B behind it is an Edit-datamodel Studio session, not a device.

rows.name: app-chrome-and-screen-gutter
rows.note: RE-POINTED 2026-08-22 (framework-gaps §8): the fixture-side pin read `Majority coverage is a judgement and it is stated as one.` out of `examples/gallery/scenarios/hud.luau`, and that sentence is gone because the RULE is gone from the consumer — `UI.Composition{ exclusions }` decides the give-way inside one `resolve` now, from the lane rects and the region widths it has in hand, and the ~90 lines of epoch token, monotone latch and per-column reserve regions were deleted with it. The pin follows the claim rather than the file: `THE RULE IS THE MEASUREMENT, NOT A FRACTION` is the same sentence in the framework's own `ResolveCtx.exclusions` block, and it still names the three coverage fractions this repository each measured wrong. THE APP DECLARES ITS OWN CHROME THROUGH THE PLATFORM.S MECHANISM (`0914c66`), plus the screen-padding gutter (`69b207f`) folded in beside it because both are the same director report and both land in tests/hud_chrome_rotation.spec.luau. ADR-0027 established that the platform.s own chrome is an L rather than a bounding box; `appChromeRects` is the app.s half of that — a list of window-space rects, empty by default, merged at exactly the point the platform.s cluster is merged, narrowing the free band only where the two genuinely overlap. THE COMPATIBILITY INVARIANT IS THE ROW.S STRONGEST CASE and it is why the feature could ship without a flag: `NOTHING declared is byte-for-byte the bounding box this HUD always spent`. A consumer that declares no chrome must be bit-identical to before, and asserting that BYTE-FOR-BYTE rather than approximately is what makes it a real guard. `a column the chrome does not cover starts LEVEL with it, not below it` is the feature itself — a 300px chip row used to cost the full width, 120px off every column; now it costs 58 where it does not cover and 120 only where it does. `the declared chrome is REPORTED as occupied` pins the env-fact contract in the other direction, so a collision check can see what the app reserved. IT IS A DECLARATION AND NEVER A MEASUREMENT, which is the source sentence pinned here, and the reason: a module that measured the app.s chrome would be measuring a ViewThatFits ladder mid-solve. THE JUDGEMENT IS STATED AS A JUDGEMENT: the fixture reserves when the chrome covers MOST of a column rather than on any overlap, and `Majority coverage is a judgement and it is stated as one.` is pinned because the alternative rules were both measured in the same session and rejected — an any-overlap rule and an anchored-edge probe — and a future author should find that on the record rather than rediscover it. THE GUTTER HALF IS NOT AN OVERFLOW BUG, WHICH IS WHY IT NEEDED ITS OWN CASES: measured live at 401x777 every right-anchored zone.s right edge was exactly 401.0 — over by 0.0px, zero collisions, flush. FLUSH IS THE DEFECT, so every overflow-only check in the repository passes on the director.s screenshot. The device leaves 1px of glass past the portrait camera and 125px past the landscape one, so one anchor-to-the-camera-edge rule reads as over-the-edge in one orientation and pulled-inward in the other; the padding is the per-edge MAX of the platform inset and the theme.s own step, and `a REAL safe-area inset still wins when it is bigger than the gutter` is the negative control that keeps MAX from silently becoming REPLACE. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM, AND IT IS A REAL WEAKNESS: the only src/ code here is environment.luau, and every assertion above runs through a FIXTURE spec rather than an env spec — a rewrite of examples/gallery/scenarios/hud.luau would take the gutter arithmetic with it, because `screenPadding` is a fixture-local memo and not a framework API. ADR-0027 was never amended to mention `appChromeRects` either; its decision record is a doc-comment in src/env/environment.luau. Both are named here rather than dressed up.

rows.name: demo-picker-mounted
rows.note: THE INSTRUMENT WAS LYING TO EVERY DEVICE PASS (`b377fe9`). `demo_picker.mountDemo` runs under a pcall, so a fixture module that threw became a client-console warn no scripted caller could see, while FacetShowcaseAPI.current happily reported the demo as up. Reproduced live by renaming a scenario module out from under the host: the API answered {current: measured-extents} over an EMPTY SCREEN. That matters more than a normal bug because this API is how every headless and Studio device sweep in this repository advances the showcase — a lying picker turns an entire device pass into a green run against nothing, and the whole gate-integrity discipline this file is built on is defeated one level below where it looks. THE FIX IS A DISTINCTION, and the row pins it as one: `current` is what was ASKED for, `mounted` is what is ON THE SCREEN (nil when the last mount failed), and the scriptable API now answers with both plus whether they agree. `the shipped scriptable API answers with what it DELIVERED, not what it was asked for` is that sentence executed. THE NEGATIVE CONTROL IS THE ROW: `a demo that cannot build is NOT reported as mounted` is the only case here that could not be satisfied by the old code, and everything else would have passed against the defect. THE SWEEP BESIDE IT IS A BROAD INVARIANT CHEAPLY: `one showNext per demo leaves EXACTLY that demo.s own screen in the tree, all 32` catches nothing-mounted, wrong-demo-mounted and previous-surface-still-standing in one assertion, and it is anchored on the catalogue so a new demo joins the sweep by existing. THE COUNT WENT 32 -> 31 ON 2026-08-16 (navigation-and-menus D8) when `table-columns` was retired into the playlist tutorial, and it is worth recording HOW that was noticed: the rename left this grep perfectly anchored and matching nothing, and `check_manifest_integrity.py --transcript` — D0.2, landed the same day — named this row and this pattern rather than letting the row quietly stop asking. It then went 31 -> 32 (D3's `callout`) and 32 -> 34 the same day, when the D2 menu and D5 tab-view fixtures joined the catalogue — both re-pointed here in the same commit as the rename, which is the discipline D0.2 exists to enforce rather than to discover. `every catalogue demo names a root screen this sweep knows to look for` is its precondition — without it a demo whose root the sweep cannot identify would be silently skipped, which is the same class of blindness one level up. THE TWO DOC GREPS pin the instruction where the next device agent will actually be standing: the verification guide and the showcase device-pass handoff both tell the reader to read `mounted`, not `current`. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: no src/ code is involved (this is entirely examples/ and the showcase host), and it says nothing about whether any given fixture is CORRECT — only that the picker.s answer about it is true.

rows.name: comparison-docs-honest
rows.note: THE TWO FRAMEWORK COMPARISONS, GATED ON THEIR HONESTY APPARATUS AND ON THEIR BUILD LEDGER — and the second half had to be REPAIRED before this row could exist, which is the finding. WHAT WAS WRONG: both documents ended in a ranked list of things to build before first release, and by 2026-08-16 three of those items had shipped while the documents still ranked them BUILD NOW. React-Lua.s Rank 1 (`UI.Foreign`, ADR-0034) and Rank 2 (the `UI.When` branch scope) read as un-built in their headings, their recommendations and the summary table, under a preamble reading `Nothing here is implemented; this is the list.` Fusion.s G-3 (`UI.sortedEntries`) read as un-built in three of four places while the section preamble already said it was built. And fusion-comparison.md carried a sentence beginning `Verified:` asserting that Enum.EasingStyle, TweenInfo and the string easing `appear nowhere in src/` — false since ADR-0033 put all three there, and worse than merely stale because the word `Verified` invites a reader to trust it without checking. THE ERROR RAN IN THE UN-BUILT DIRECTION IN EVERY CASE: neither document claimed anything shipped that had not. That is the benign direction for a vendor comparison and the malignant one for a work list, because the next mission reads it and rebuilds what exists. FIXED IN THIS STAGE, minimally: the three items now carry the same struck-BUILD-NOW / BUILT marker G-1 already used, the preamble names what shipped, and the easing paragraph is re-tensed as a before picture with its own correction. THE ROW GATES BOTH DIRECTIONS. Forward: `BUILT 2026-08-15` must be present in both files. Backward, and this is the part a grep-for-presence could not do: three NEGATIVE assertions refuse the specific stale strings that were just removed, so a revert, a bad merge or a well-meaning tidy that restores `Nothing here is implemented`, a bare `Rank 1 ... BUILD NOW` heading, or the false `appear nowhere in src/` sentence reddens this row instead of sitting there being read. THE HONESTY APPARATUS IS THE OTHER HALF and it is what makes these documents worth having at all: two verification appendices listing what could NOT be verified. Five sentences are pinned by hand — that no Fusion project was ever built for the comparison, that a citation proves a sentence and not a behaviour, that no physical-device evidence exists on Facet.s side, that the document lives in Facet.s own repository and that is a structural reason to distrust it, that nothing on the React-Lua side was executed, that no citation in it is mechanically checked, and that Facet.s own performance figures were carried over rather than re-run. Those are exactly the paragraphs a later editor deletes as hedging, and deleting them converts a careful survey into marketing. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: that any comparison in either document is CORRECT. Neither is among the nine check_docs reads, so no citation in either is mechanically verified — the row pins that this limitation is still DISCLOSED, which is the only thing a gate can honestly do about it.

rows.name: source-size-cap
rows.note: THE 200,000-CHARACTER `Script.Source` CAP, AND THIS ROW EXISTS BECAUSE NOTHING RAN THE CHECKER. tools/check_source_size.py has been in the tree, passing, and mutation-proven to bite since round 3 — and the only mention of it in this entire manifest was `test -f tools/check_source_size.py` inside the round-3 owed ledger. A `test -f` on an executable check is the cheapest possible pretence of coverage: the file could have been truncated to a shebang and every gate in this repository would still have been green. It is wired now. WHY THE CAP IS REAL RATHER THAN AESTHETIC: Roblox refuses a `Script.Source` write past roughly 200k characters, so a module that crosses it stops SYNCING into Studio — the failure is silent, it looks like a stale place rather than a size limit, and this repository has already lost time to exactly that diagnosis. THE ROW ASSERTS TWO THINGS, NOT ONE. First that the checker PASSES. Second, in its own inline Python, that `KNOWN_OVER` is still EMPTY — and that second assertion is the whole point, because `KNOWN_OVER` is the waiver list and a checker with a populated waiver list passes trivially. Round 4 emptied it: row_actions came down 234,757 -> 183,738 and renderer 242,943 -> 175,901, and with the list empty every module in src/ is guarded normally and any file that reaches the cap fails on the run that crosses it. Gating the PASS without gating the emptiness would let a future agent make this row green again by adding a line, which is the failure mode a waiver list always has. The checker.s own ratchet is stricter still and is left to it: a listed file that GREW fails, and a listed file that SHRANK also fails, asking for its ceiling to be lowered so progress cannot silently reverse. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: nothing about tests/, tools/, examples/ or bench/, which the checker does not read; and nothing about whether any module is comprehensible at its current size, which is the architecture question the cap only approximates.

It anchors on `<name> = ` now, the baseline still passes, and the mutation bites. Fourth instance of that class recorded on 2026-08-16; the defect it guards, a checker whose own suggested auto-fix would delete the three metrics, is booked as CR-1 in artifacts/swiftui-parity-round4/carried-reds.md. SPELLED FAIL_ENVIRONMENT WITH releaseBlocking = false, this manifest.s established shape for work blocked on hardware or a human session: it reads as a non-PASS in the roll-up and in gate.json, it is visible to anyone reading the gate, and it does not block the phase — while a bare PENDING would make the gate structurally un-passable and would therefore get deleted rather than closed.

rows.name: authored-presentation-composition
rows.note: ADR-0026, AND THE DECISION IS THAT AN AUTHORED VALUE IS A TERM, NOT A SECOND WRITER. `opacity`, `scale` and `rotation` are authorable, and the obvious implementation gives the author a second authority over the same three engine properties the presentation channel already owns — which is how two writers fight over one property and the last one to run wins. The ADR refuses that and composes instead, and the sentence pinned here is the whole of it: `the authored value is an INPUT to the presentation authority, never a writer`. `The manifest does not change. Not one line.` is the consequence a future author is most likely to erode, because adding an authority is the easy way to add a feature. THE THREE COMPOSITION LAWS ARE PINNED AS ARITHMETIC, not as prose: opacity MULTIPLIES (0.5 under 0.5 paints 0.25), scale MULTIPLIES (2 under 1.5 paints 3), rotation ADDS (30 under 15 paints 45). Each is a number a mutation cannot satisfy by accident, and they are deliberately not the same operator — a single generic compose would get one of the three wrong. THE TWO NEGATIVE CONTROLS ARE WHAT MAKE THE ROW MORE THAN THREE MULTIPLICATIONS: `clearing the FRAMEWORK.s contribution leaves the AUTHORED value standing` proves the terms are genuinely separable rather than collapsed into one number at write time, and `a surface authoring NONE of the three writes no presentation property at all` is the off-path cost claim — the feature costs nothing on every surface that does not use it. `NESTED groups do NOT double-compose` is the boundary between the two composers: the engine multiplies ACROSS nodes, the framework composes WITHIN one, and a framework that also multiplied across nodes would square the fade on every nested group. THE PRESS-DIP HALF IS A REAL SHIPPED BUG (`5004777`) AND IT IS THE STRONGEST PAIR HERE: a button with an authored scale lost it on press, because the dip wrote an ABSOLUTE target instead of a relative one. `NO press-dip target in screen_paint is an absolute 1 — every one derives from the resting scale` is the fix as an invariant over all four sites, and `...and all FOUR sites read it through one named helper, not four literals` is the ENGINEERING.md grep-every-caller rule executed — fixing the site the report named and leaving three siblings absolute would satisfy any single-site assertion. `The dip is a relative gesture, and always meant to be.` is that reading put on the record so the next author does not re-derive it as absolute. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: nothing on a device, and nothing about the game — Rascal Rally uses none of the three (its own ADR rider says so), so there is deliberately NO game-side half here and inventing one would be a contract test with no consumer behind it.

rows.name: cross-surface-overlap
rows.note: ADR-0028. TWO SURFACES CAN OVERLAP ON PURPOSE, AND THE ONLY THING THAT SEPARATES A BUG FROM A DESIGN IS WHAT SOMEBODY DECLARED — which is why `the alarm reads DECLARATIONS, not geometry` is the pinned sentence and why the naive implementation (intersect the rects, report) is wrong rather than merely noisy. A modal over a screen intersects completely and is correct; a toast over a HUD intersects and is correct; two screens in the same band intersecting is a defect. THE DECLARATION VOCABULARY IS PINNED ITEM BY ITEM because each one is a different way to get it wrong: a different BAND is a declaration (`a MODAL over a base screen reports nothing`), `edgeToEdge` on EITHER side is a declaration (a scrim means to cover AND to be covered — the either-side half is what a one-sided check misses), and `the four SURFACE_LAYER bands land in four DISTINCT bands` pins that the presenter.s own table and this scan agree, so a band added to one and not the other is a failure rather than a silent hole. THE TWO NON-DECLARATIONS ARE THE SHARPER HALF: `deviceSafeContent is NOT a declaration — it is an inset choice, not a layering one` and `an UNSET display order declares nothing`. Both are things that LOOK like layering intent, and treating either as consent is how an alarm goes quiet on exactly the defect it exists for. `What is deliberately NOT a declaration` pins that list in the ADR. THE OPACITY TRIPLE IS THE BEST EVIDENCE THIS IS NOT A GEOMETRY CHECK, and it is a three-case set on purpose: a surface at `opacity = 0` covers nothing (and the case says out loud that a geometry-only test WOULD report it), a framework fade to nothing covers nothing (the same rule reached through the other contributor — ADR-0026.s composition, which is why these two ADRs are neighbours), and `at any opacity above zero it covers again` is the negative control that stops `never report a faded surface` from satisfying the first two. `coverRect is the union of what a surface paints BELOW its root` is the geometry half done right: a root.s own rect is a claim, not a paint. THE COST DISCIPLINE IS A ROW OF ITS OWN INSIDE THIS ONE: `a frame NEVER scans` plus `a single-surface target does not scan even when it IS read` pin that this is an INSPECTION API and not a solve-time finding — nothing runs per frame, and the trivial case is free. The lifecycle pair (exit transitions leave immediately, disposal leaves the REGISTRY) is the leak direction: a bucket that grows with every mount would turn an inspection into an O(mounts) scan. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: the game-side half lives in the rascalrally-consumer row.s own contract spec, and no Studio capture was taken of two genuinely colliding surfaces.

rows.name: leaf-opacity-refusal
rows.note: ADR-0029, THE SIBLING REFUSAL TO ADR-0026, AND THE ONLY ROW IN THIS BLOCK WHOSE EVERY CASE IS A REFUSAL OR A NEGATIVE CONTROL. ADR-0026 made `opacity` composable; the obvious next step is to offer it on a leaf, and it is refused. THE REASON IS THE SAME MECHANIC THE TINT-FILL ROW IS ABOUT, from the other side: under native stylesheets a leaf.s transparency is SHEET-OWNED, and writing it takes the base term away — `GetStyled` then returns the write, so there is nothing left to compose against and the sheet.s own state rules (disabled dim above all) stop applying. `the leaf fade stays refused, because a composition has no base term to compose against` is that in one sentence and it is pinned. THE REFUSAL IS A CONSTRUCTION ERROR THAT NAMES THE FIX, which is this codebase.s established shape and is asserted in three separate ways: it names the defeat (the disabled dimming it would break), it names the WORKAROUND spelled out rather than pointing at a doc, and `canvasGroup` on a leaf gets the SAME message — one fact, both spellings, because a refusal that only covers one of two names for the same thing is half a refusal. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE CASE THAT KEEPS THIS HONEST: `opacity` is on exactly TWO classes and every other one refuses it BY NAME, which is a closed statement about the whole class table rather than a spot check, and its counterpart `scale and rotation are offered on EVERY rendered class and refused on none` proves the refusal is about the SHEET-OWNED property and not a general nervousness about authored presentation — neither transform touches anything the sheet owns, so neither is refused. `a STRUCTURAL class is not given the fade refusal — it has no instance to fade` is the boundary of the boundary: five classes are deliberately excluded because refusing a property on a thing that has no instance would be a confusing error, and the ADR says so. TWO CONTROLS STOP THIS FROM BEING A REFUSAL THAT SWALLOWS EVERYTHING: `a genuinely unknown property is UNCHANGED — the refusal did not swallow the suggester` (the did-you-mean path still works, which a naive early-return would have eaten) and `the refusal is on the ERROR PATH ONLY — one caller, and it is the failing constructor`, which is the cost claim: this machinery runs only when a construction is already failing. `the wrap fades the GROUP and writes nothing at all on the control inside it` is the named workaround executed, so the row proves the escape route works rather than merely that the door is shut. THE DOMAIN IS REFUSED RATHER THAN CLAMPED, at both the literal and the REACTIVE read site — the second is the one that matters, because a bound value leaving the domain later is the case a construction-time check cannot see. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: nothing about how the engine actually resolves a competing write — that is the GetStyled measurement in artifacts/adr-0029-leaf-opacity/live-probes.md, a Studio session, not anything this row re-runs.

rows.name: nested-instance-tree
rows.note: ADR-0032 IS BUILT NOW, AND THIS ROW REPLACES THE DEFERRAL ROW THAT ASKED TO BE REPLACED. Its predecessor (`nested-instance-tree-deferred`) deliberately ran NO suite grep, on the reasoning that the clip-host cases it might have pinned were PRE-EXISTING behaviour the ADR merely observed, so greping them would credit this ADR with somebody else.s work and keep passing if the ADR were deleted outright. That reasoning was right and it ended the moment the migration landed; the old row.s closing sentence said so itself: `if nesting is ever built, this row should be replaced by one that runs the real thing`. WHAT IS PINNED NOW, and every one of these is work this round did rather than observed. THE REGISTRY: `registerHost` exists as the ONE registration site, which is what makes `which paths get registered` -- the single predicate the whole migration changes -- have one place to live. `hostFor` is pinned BY COST rather than by shape, because the two implementations are indistinguishable by result: 20,000 lookups against 4,001 hosts, scan 4.9485 s versus walk 0.0077 s, bounded in the suite at 2.0 s. That is the check that decides whether `register more hosts` is affordable at all, and it would have failed silently as the feature arrived. THE ARRANGE HALF: the minimal-write contract (`handle.lastWriteX ~= px`), the deferred re-base (`adapter.settleRects`), and the document-order rect pass, all three of which are needed together -- the write skip alone was MEASURED delivering nothing, because the two writes it was meant to collapse were two DIFFERENT values. The A/A and no-host cases are pinned beside the headline case deliberately: without them `never write anything` passes every one of these. THE BOUNDARY PREDICATE: a container with an authored scale/rotation becomes a real parent, a rotated LEAF does not, and `crops` is distinguished from `clipChildren` -- a CanvasGroup crops without ever setting that property, because its buffer is its own size, and conflating them would grow a focus-ring float under every container that merely moves. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT PINNED HERE. The engine claims. That a plain Frame carries Rotation and UIScale to its descendants, that the descendant.s own properties stay untouched, and that 240 descendant Position changes became 0 are all STUDIO measurements; this row checks only that their evidence file is on disk and carries the number. A gate cannot re-run an engine, and a headless grep that reads like an engine claim is how this project has shipped defects before -- so the artifact is the witness and it is cited, not re-derived. `check_elision_census` IS run, because that one is headless and is the number most likely to be given back quietly: it holds the flat 20-row list at exactly 142 creates / 61 elided / 81 GuiObjects and charges Decision 4 its +20 instances on the rotated fixture. DECISION 6 AND DECISION 3 ARE CARRIED OVER UNCHANGED from the deferral row, and for the same reasons: nothing in src/ may CONSTRUCT a UIListLayout/UIGridLayout/UITableLayout/UIPageLayout (the check greps `Instance.new` rather than the bare names, which is load-bearing -- all four names legitimately appear in comments and refusal messages explaining why the framework does not use them), and `ZIndexBehavior.Sibling` stays pinned because Decision 3 rests on it and a switch to Global is the specific reversal that would make a nested tree behave differently than measured.
