rows.name: core-settle-phase
rows.note: `core:settle` — A NEW PHASE OF THE REACTIVE CORE, and the largest thing round 4 shipped that the first pass of this gate missed entirely. Terminal work registered through `core:settle` runs AFTER propagation quiesces, in registration order; a callback that WRITES ends the pass, lets propagation drain, and the pass RESTARTS from the first callback; passes repeat until one writes nothing. That restart is the whole mechanism and it is what the first case asserts — a settle phase that ran its callbacks once would look correct in every single-write test and would leave the second-order write for the next frame, which is precisely the defect this closes. THE CONFORMANCE CASES RUN AGAINST ALL THREE SUBSTRATES (custom, fusion adapter, imperative), which is why they are pinned by their hyphenated conformance names rather than by prose: a phase added to one substrate and not the others is a core contract that is not a contract. `settle-callbacks-never-see-a-half-propagated-graph` is the ordering guarantee that makes the phase usable at all, and `settle-unsubscribe-is-idempotent-and-counter-neutral` is the leak direction. CONVERGENCE IS BOUNDED, NOT HOPED FOR: `settle-that-never-converges-hits-the-iteration-cap` and `a round trip that will not converge is a LOUD error, not a hang or a silent frame` are the same rule from the core side and the consumer side. A settle pass counts against the existing `FEEDBACK_ROUND_CAP`, so a non-converging cycle is a quarantined error rather than a frozen client — the failure mode a naive fixpoint loop ships with. THE CONSUMER IS THE MEASURE-PUBLISH ROUND TRIP, and its cases carry their own control, which is what makes them worth gating: `the round trip costs NO extra reactive flush — the control is in the case` runs the same scene with the publication removed, in the same process, so a change that slowed BOTH arms cannot pass it. `a surface is FINAL when the geometry change returns — no correction a frame later` is the player-visible half (a reservation that lands one frame late is a visible jump), and `...and the published reservation is REALLY applied — the fix is not .never publish.` is the negative control without which deleting the publication entirely would satisfy the first. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: the device numbers. The commit records a headless steady state reproducing a device capture to three significant figures (3 react / 7 arrange / 2 mount, becoming 2 / 6 / 1), but those are tier-1 counts against a tier-3 observation and this row re-measures neither — it pins the CONTRACT (converges in one flush, bounded, substrate-uniform), which is the portable half.

rows.name: virtual-grid-family
rows.note: THE GRID FAMILY: `UI.Grid { flow }` (eager, column-major as a MODE) and `newVirtualGrid { axis }` (vertical grid and sideways grid, windowed). THE CLAIM WORTH GATING IS THAT NEITHER ADDED A SECOND ARITHMETIC, and it is pinned three ways because it is the claim that decays first. `every cell.s rect is the row-flow rect with both axes exchanged` is the transpose asserted as an EQUALITY against the row-flow answer rather than against frozen numbers — a hand-written column layout would drift from it the first time either mode changed. `grid.measure and grid.arrange both call the SAME flow plan` closes the classic seam where a layout is right at arrange and wrong at measure. `the solver keeps no grid arithmetic of its own — it only holds the cache.s home` is the structural half, and the two parity-document greps pin the decision in reader-facing prose (`a MODE of one arithmetic, not a second layout`; `The control gained an axis without gaining any arithmetic`). `.flow. on a ROW grid is a diagnostic, not a second layout` is the negative control: the prop is READ in exactly one mode and is otherwise reported rather than silently accepted, which is the accepted-and-ignored class this repo has been bitten by. THE LAZINESS CASES ARE PER-AXIS ON PURPOSE, and the two chosen are the ones that DISAMBIGUATE: `the build count does not depend on N — 100 items and 10 000 build the same cells` is the vertical grid.s and `...and the build count is INDEPENDENT OF N — the property .only as needed. names` is the horizontal one. The obvious case title (`10 000 items, 4 lanes: the EXACT cells of the windowed lines are built and no others`) appears VERBATIM IN BOTH virtual_grid.spec and virtual_hgrid.spec, so a grep on it matches twice and cannot tell a working V grid from a broken H grid — it is deliberately not used here, and that is worth recording because an ambiguous grep is a row that half-passes silently. `the canvas extent IS virtual_extents.uniform over ceil(N / lanes) lines — a differential` is the strongest single case in the row: it checks the grid against the shared index rather than against a number, so the grid and the list cannot drift apart, and it pins the UNIT (LINES, not items) that a lane-count bug gets wrong. `when the COLUMN COUNT changes, the item at the top of the viewport stays at the top` is the only case here a player would notice. THE REFUSALS bound the axis: `width` refused on the horizontal axis WITH the route, an axis that is neither refused naming the legal pair, a non-integer column count refused, and a mix of rows and loose cells refused. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: the two pure lifts that rode along (`virtual_window`, `virtual_reorder`) are NOT gated — they produce no case name of their own by design, their registry entries say so, and a row asserting a file exists would be the `test -f` this stage already removed once.

rows.name: variable-item-extents
rows.note: VARIABLE AND MEASURED ITEM EXTENTS — AND THIS IS THE ROW THAT CLOSES THE LYING-`itemExtent` PROBLEM THE ROUND-3 GATE HAS A WHOLE ROW ABOUT. Round 3 shipped a DIAGNOSTIC for a consumer that mispredicts its own row height; round 4 removed the prediction. `itemExtent` now takes four forms (a number, a Readable, a per-item function, and `measured`), and the fourth makes the row.s extent what its own cell MEASURED. THE STRUCTURAL CLOSURE IS PINNED AS A PAIR, and it is the most interesting thing here: `the cell that makes the guard shout under a DECLARATION produces no finding here` — the same cell, the same guard, silent, because a measured list makes no prediction to lie about. Beside it `A FIXED ROW STOPS BEING REPORTED — the finding does not outlive the defect` is the stale-finding half, which is a real failure mode for any diagnostic that caches. THE COMPATIBILITY LADDER IS THREE SEPARATE EQUALITIES because the old path must not move: every question agrees when every extent is equal; a per-item function returning one constant is IDENTICAL to the uniform list; and a measured list of equal rows CONVERGES to the uniform list declaring that number. Together they say the three new forms are refinements of the old arithmetic rather than a second one, which is the same standing rule the grid row carries. CONVERGENCE IS ONE STEP, NOT A LOOP, and that is a design consequence rather than luck: the cell rides one control-owned wrapper sized `content` on the scroll axis, so it CANNOT see the slot it decides, and `convergence is ONE step: a second refresh over the same content writes nothing` is that asserted. Without it a measured list is a feedback loop, which is the failure `core:settle` exists to bound. THE BOUNDS: a logarithmic number of extent reads on 10,000 items, a window that never grows with the list, no trailing gutter in the content extent, and `mid-slot, the variable rule windows one MORE row — and that is deliberate` (a deliberate over-mount named as such, so a later reader does not tighten it as a bug). THE REFUSALS keep the fourth form closed: any other string, an estimate on a list that does not measure (an accepted property that drives nothing is constitution §4), a non-positive per-item extent, and a `fill` cell on the scroll axis — with `a DECLARED list still accepts a fill cell` as the control proving the refusal belongs to measured mode alone. THE LAST GREP IS A DOC CORRECTION MADE BY THIS STAGE: the comparison table still listed measured extents as `Missing — the named next stage, not started`, five days after they shipped. It now records them as covered, and the row asserts both the new text AND the ABSENCE of the old `but never ask the row` phrase, so a revert reddens rather than sitting there telling the next mission to build what exists. Same class as the comparison-docs row, found the same way.

rows.name: text-line-box
rows.note: THE LINE BOX: ONE PUBLIC ANSWER TO `how tall is N lines`, AND THREE DEFECTS OUT OF THE PUBLIC FUNCTION THAT USED TO ANSWER IT. A 2026-08 survey found SEVEN near-duplicates of this formula in the repository and exactly ONE of them correct — and the correct one was private to a gallery fixture while the public `composition.floorPx` was wrong three ways. `When three consumers make an identical mistake the API is wrong, not the consumers` is the pinned sentence and it is the reason this shipped as an API rather than as three bug fixes. THE THREE DEFECTS ARE PINNED INDIVIDUALLY, BY NUMBER, because each is separately re-introducible and each has a different blast radius. DEFECT 1, no `ceil`: a floor of 16.8 against a measured 17 let a region hold one line legally in a box that cannot draw it. DEFECT 2, no SCALE: `role.size` is the AUTHORED size, so on ten-foot and raised-preference the floor was short by up to 3x — an accessibility defect invisible at the default. DEFECT 3, no TEXT OFFSET: at the four offsets this project binds itself to, a one-line floor was short by 16.8px and a four-line floor by 67.2px. THE TWO COMPOSITION INVARIANTS ARE THE SUBTLE HALF and are what a re-implementation gets wrong even knowing the three defects: `THE CEIL LANDS ONCE, on the whole product — not per line` (ceiling per line accumulates error linearly) and `the offset is ADDITIVE and lands AFTER the scale, never through it`, with `the offset.s marginal cost does NOT depend on the scale` as the invariant form of the same statement — the case that fails if somebody folds the offset into the size before scaling, which produces plausible numbers everywhere except at the extremes. `a SUB-1 preference reserves at the PAINT scale, never at the smaller one` is the reserve-generously direction chosen deliberately. THE ONE-IMPLEMENTATION CLAIM IS ASSERTED STRUCTURALLY: `is the solver.s own two seams, composed in the solver.s order` — `lineBox` CALLS `text_metrics.reservedSize` and `lineBoxPx`, the same two functions the render path spends, so changing either seam moves the prediction with it. `every row: the predicted line box IS the arranged rect, and the predicted reserved size IS the solve.s` is that closed against a real solve. THE ENV REFUSAL is a reactivity trap worth its own case: `{ env } WITHOUT use is refused — a fact read with :get() is right once and then stale`, which is the accessibility bug this whole feature is about, re-introduced through the API.s own front door. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM, AND THE RECORD IS EXPLICIT: the spec.s generated-corpus differential does NOT cover the two primitives. Because `lineBox` calls the solver.s seams rather than reproducing them, mutating a primitive moves prediction and measurement together and the differential stays silent — its job is the COMPOSITION (which scale, which offset, which role, which order), and the concrete-number cases are what pin the primitives. Pretending otherwise would be claiming an oracle that does not fire.

rows.name: measure-memo-key
rows.note: L-37, AND IT IS A CACHE-KEY DEFECT — THE CLASS THIS MANIFEST ALREADY CARRIES A WARNING ABOUT. The round-3 flow-wrap note records that a key which does not cover what it caches returns a STALE CORRECT-LOOKING number no geometry assertion above it can see. This is the same family from the opposite direction: the per-solve measure memo.s key carried `maxH`, the OFFERED height, on nodes whose measured size provably cannot read it, so the key was unique per offer and the memo never hit. Instrumented per node on a 30-deep arm: 16.33 distinct `maxH` against 1.00 distinct `maxW` and 1.00 distinct scope key — the one field that made every key unique was the one field the computation ignored. That measurement is pinned as a literal in the source comment, because it is the evidence the rule rests on. SO THE ROW HAD TO BE BUILT ON AN ORACLE RATHER THAN ON GEOMETRY, and it is: `...and the fan-out does not RISE with depth, which is the whole defect` and `a 30-deep chain measures each node about twice, not sixteen times` read the framework.s own `work.measured` COUNTER off the public result. The number under test IS the cache-miss count, so a stale-but-correct-looking answer is visible here in a way it never is through a rect. THE THREE EXCLUSIONS ARE THE CORRECTNESS HALF and each is pinned separately, because dropping the offer from the key is only sound where the answer genuinely cannot read it: a `hug` height READS the offer, a `vwrap` breaks its lines ON the offered height, and a child that can be SQUEEZED makes its vertical stack read it too. Each was mutated separately against a differential oracle over 800 seeded trees (25,961 node comparisons, zero differences for the shipped rule; the over-broad rule diverges on 2,933) and transcribed as a biting case pinned by the rect the mutation moves. THE VERDICT REPLAY IS THE PART A RECT CANNOT SEE: `the memo does not move geometry — the verdicts are the only thing at risk` names the real hazard, and the two seeded cases pin it — a cut label must still report `truncated = true` so its disclosure path survives, and a compact label that does not fit must keep its compact verdict. Both are byte-identical in geometry and different in behaviour, which is exactly the defect a geometry suite cannot catch. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM, AND THE RECORD SAYS IT FIRST: `PLAN_SKIP`, the third rule, has NO correctness coverage — its own mutation ledger records that deleting the branch reddens NOTHING, and its only evidence is an interleaved A/B. It is not pinned here and must not be read as covered. Nor are the percentages: the -82.5% on the deep arm is a headless bench figure stated with its A/A control, and this row re-measures none of it.

rows.name: table-virtualized
rows.note: `newTable { virtualized = true }` — THE RICH CONTAINER WINDOWS. This is Table, not Grid, and it is the harder of the two because a Table carries columns, a header, resizable widths and multi-range selection, all of which have opinions about rows that are not mounted. THREE HAND-ROLLED O(N) ROW-GEOMETRY LOOPS COLLAPSED INTO ONE `virtual_extents` PREFIX SUM shared with `newVirtualList` — and, importantly, for the FLOWING table too, which is why the measured -95.4% (three order-swapped rounds against a +/-3% A/A band) lands on a path nobody was virtualizing: the old `contentHeight()` was O(N) per call and `clampScroll` called it. THE STATE-VS-WINDOW CASES ARE THE POINT OF THIS ROW, because they are what a list does not have to answer. `a drag while scrolled names a slot two hundred rows down, not a window-relative one` is the index-space bug every windowed reorder ships first. `multi-selection ranges reach rows the window never held` is the same hazard for selection: a range is a statement about the DATA, and a windowed implementation that resolves it against mounted rows silently truncates it. `a FLOWING table.s row tops agree with the same index` closes the seam between the two modes, so the paths cannot drift. `FRAME ONE already fills the body: the seed is the screen, so it over-mounts, never under` is one of two defects the mission.s own mutation testing found, and the direction is deliberate — an under-mounted first frame is a visibly empty table for one frame, an over-mounted one is invisible. `a text-preference change RE-SOLVES the rows, never rebuilds them` is the accessibility axis crossed with virtualization, which is where round 3.s large-text findings kept landing. `...and WITHOUT the anchor the same change would move it — the guard is not decorative` is the negative control that stops the scroll-anchor case from being satisfied by a table that simply never moves. THE TWO REFUSALS ARE PREREQUISITES, NOT OMISSIONS: `virtualized` with `scrolls = false` is refused because a block table has no viewport to window against, and `virtualized` with `rowActions` is refused in v1 the same way VirtualList refuses reorder plus rowActions — a refusal with a stated reason, which is this codebase.s shape for deferring rather than half-building. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: the -95.4% (a headless bench figure, not re-measured here), and nothing on a device — a windowed table.s scroll feel is exactly the kind of thing only a finger can judge, and no Play session was available.

rows.name: hud-composition-collisions
rows.note: ADR-0025.S HUD COMPOSITION, FINISHED: `holdsLane`, a group `align` across the lane, and `resolution.collisions`. A screen-anchored HUD is a PARTITION — nine anchors that divide the screen and by construction cannot overlap — and this row is about the two places that construction is not enough. `holdsLane` IS RULE 9.S COUNTERPART AND ITS NUMBER IS THE ARGUMENT: an empty centre column released its third, which is right for a page and exactly wrong where the lane POSITIONS are the coordinate system — measured before the flag, an empty centre column moved the whole right-hand cluster 150px left. `an empty centre column keeps its third and the right cluster does not move` is that fixed, and `without the flag the lane still releases — rule 9 is unchanged` is the negative control that makes it an opt-in rather than a silent behaviour change for every existing composition. `holdsLane is refused on a spanning group — a span row has no lane to hold` is the refusal that keeps the flag meaningful. THE COLLISION ALARM IS FOR THE ONE FAILURE A PARTITION CANNOT REMOVE, and this is the part worth reading: a region whose FORM measures bigger than the box the partition gave it paints on its neighbour while the composition itself stays perfectly legal — so no existing fallback finding fires, and the screen is wrong with a green solve. `a zone wider than its column names the zone it is painting over` is the alarm, offender named first so the finding is actionable. IT IS GATED BY A PROPER CONTROL PAIR: `a well-behaved HUD reports NO collisions` and `a wide zone with nothing beside it is not a collision` — without the second, `report every wide zone` would satisfy the first, and an alarm that fires on legal layouts gets disabled, which is worse than not shipping it. `the SCROLL region is excluded — its content is meant to be bigger than its box` is the one principled exemption, the same exception the round-3 virtual-slot guard needed. THE DEGRADATION ORDER IS PINNED AS A POLICY, not as an outcome: the least important zone in the failing column gives way FIRST, a column that runs out of forms drops its droppable zone AND NO OTHER, and a zone that was never in the failing column keeps its richest form. Those three together are what stop a single over-wide zone from cascading a whole HUD down its fallback ladder — the failure mode where one bad measurement makes every readout ugly at once. `no two zones intersect, at any height a landscape phone can lose` is the invariant swept across the shape that actually breaks HUDs. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: the 150px is a recorded measurement, not re-measured here; and this is a headless partition claim — whether the resulting HUD READS well on a phone is a human judgement no gate row can make.

rows.name: table-gutter-and-divider-press
rows.note: TWO TABLE DEFECTS THE HIT-EXPANDER ROW DOES NOT REACH, both found on a device and both about a press or a pixel landing somewhere nobody declared. THE GUTTER: a Y-scrolling body reserves 8px for its scrollbar and the HEADER did not, so every header cell sat 8px wide of its own column — measured byte-for-byte as `header best: 630..895` against a body window ending at 887, the bar occupying 887..895. The fix publishes the reserve from the solver KEYED BY THE SIDE IT CAME OFF, and the axis pair is why the first two greps exist: an X shelf reports on `bottom` and a Y list on `right`, which is the transpose a single-axis implementation gets wrong and no vertical test can see. `The drift IS the reserve` is the measurement pinned in source — a headless A/B over the swept viewports gave 8px of worst-case drift with the reserve and 0px without, which is what turns this from a plausible story into a fix. THE THREE SILENCE CASES ARE THE HALF THAT KEEPS IT HONEST: a host whose content FITS publishes nothing, a fallback adapter with no bar publishes nothing, and an unmounted host stops answering — without them `always reserve 8` would satisfy the positive cases and would cost a gutter on every table that never scrolls. `...and with no bar to reserve, the same grid, and no gutter paid` is that same control at the Table level, and `PRESENT ALONE lands the grids together — the gutter costs no frame at all` pins that the correction happens within the first present rather than one frame later, which is the visible-jump class `core:settle` exists for. `WHY PADDING AND NOT A TRAILING SPACER CHILD` pins the alternative that was considered and rejected, so the next author does not re-open it. THE DIVIDER PRESS IS A SEPARATE MECHANISM FROM THE Z RULE, and pairing them in one row would have hidden that: the hit-expander row makes the 44px band REACHABLE, this one makes a press inside it that is NOT a drag do the right thing. `a press and release with no travel sorts the column and commits NO width` is the defect — a click at (264,134) previously did NOTHING because the expander claimed it and the grip never used it. The press is now re-dispatched to what was underneath, `within` the cell and `skip`ping the grip so it cannot forward to itself. `travel UNDER the pointer promotion gate is still a tap; travel over it is a resize` is the boundary asserted from both sides, and `the guide line does not appear for a press that never becomes a drag` is the visible consequence. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: `api.columnWidthOverrides` becoming a Readable shipped no test of its own and is deliberately NOT pinned; and both device measurements behind this row were taken by a human in a session, not re-run here.

rows.name: d0-one-run-per-sweep
rows.note: D0.1. A full sweep ran the Facet suite 234 times and the RascalRally suite 67 times to grep 1127 lines out of byte-identical transcripts. MEASURED on this machine: 83.4 s a Facet run, 36.5 s a RascalRally run — the better part of four hours per sweep regenerating two files. `tools/test.sh` now owns a cache keyed on a CONTENT fingerprint (src/ tests/ examples/ vendor/ + the toolchain pins + the lune version) and `tools/suite_transcript.sh` is the thin front door every check greps; RascalRally has its own, whose fingerprint ALSO covers GameStudio/ui/Facet/{src,tests} because its specs require Facet modules directly. THIS ROW IS THE STRUCTURAL HALF: check_manifest_integrity now REFUSES a run string that invokes `./run-tests.sh` directly (one of those costs 83 s a sweep and re-opens the four hours this stage closed), both helpers are executable, both actually serve a transcript carrying a pass marker and a summary line, and both report a cache HIT afterwards — which is what proves the serve did not re-run. The behavioural half, where every guard is broken on purpose, is `d0-cache-guards-bite`. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: the three remaining `./run-tests.sh` mentions in this file are prose in `note` strings describing a run inside a `git archive` scratch directory — a DIFFERENT tree, where this tree's cache must not be used, so they are correct as written.

rows.name: d0-cache-guards-bite
rows.note: D0.1's guards, each asserted by BREAKING IT. A cache is exactly the shape that turns a real check into one that cannot fail — serve a stale or red transcript and 1127 gate greps become decoration in one commit — so the gate-integrity sweep's standing rule (a check is worthless until a mutation has been seen to fail it, ledger C-08) applies here more than anywhere. 27 assertions across five groups: the fingerprint is CONTENT (a new file, an edited file, and a restored file each move it, and a changed tree reports `miss` without running anything); hit-or-run never trust-the-file (absent cache, missing meta, and a foreign fingerprint all report `miss`); THE EXIT CODE RIDES WITH THE TRANSCRIPT (red, failing, truncated, fast-tier, empty, and mutated-after-caching are each refused, and each refusal asserts BOTH a non-zero exit — which reddens FORM A's `&&` chain — AND empty stdout, which is the only thing that can redden a FORM B pipeline whose exit status is grep's); a valid cache is served verbatim and a warm call rewrites nothing and costs 0 s against an 83 s suite; and the RascalRally half, including the one that matters most for consumer lockstep — a Facet `src/` edit MUST move the RascalRally fingerprint, or the game suite serves a stale green over a broken consumer. TWO MUTATIONS WERE RUN AGAINST THE IMPLEMENTATION ITSELF and both were caught: making the helper serve regardless of validity reddened 6 assertions, and keying the fingerprint on `date` instead of content reddened 2. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: it does not re-prove that the suites themselves are correct, only that a transcript may not be trusted without earning it.

rows.name: d0-greps-still-match
rows.note: D0.2. `check_manifest_integrity.py` enforced that every suite grep is ANCHORED to the pass marker, which is a SYNTACTIC property — it never ran the suite, so it could not know whether the pattern still matches a line that exists. Rename a spec case and the grep stays perfectly anchored and matches nothing; the gate reddens only when somebody runs that gate, at 83 s a go. Two consecutive stages found exactly that by hand (round 4's own note ends: `an argument for a checker that replays every suite grep in this file against a live transcript, and that checker does not exist yet`). It exists now, and D0.1's cached transcript is what made it free. 1127 patterns replayed, all matched. FOUR TRAPS, ALL HIT WHILE BUILDING IT: (1) `grep`, never `grep -E` — the manifest is BRE, and under ERE a pattern like `traverse(+1)` is a syntax error whose exit 2 reads as `no match`, which inflated the brief's own first count from 13 to 95; (2) route each pattern to the transcript ITS OWN CAPTURE came from, positionally — a check may capture `$out` from Facet and only THEN `cd` into RascalRally, and a subshell `(cd RR && …)` hands the tail back to Facet; (3) a negated grep asserts an absence, so zero matches is its point and it is excluded; (4) FINDING NOTHING IS A FAILURE — when the manifest moved off `./run-tests.sh` this script's own discovery regex went quiet and printed `0 suite greps, all anchored`, green and proving nothing, which MIN_EXPECTED_GREPS now floors at 900. THE BRIEF'S `13 STALE PATTERNS` WERE MOSTLY TRAP 2, MEASURED HERE: 65 of the 1127 patterns belong to RascalRally, and 63 of those match nothing in the Facet transcript — mis-route them and you report 63 false positives. Replaying the manifest AS OF 37e9dad found exactly ONE genuinely stale pattern (`large-text-accessibility` / `overflow-policy`, the LT6-ACTION title renamed by 4a948d0), and HEAD had already re-pointed it by hand. So the count at HEAD is 0 and the check lands green rather than red on arrival. MUTATION PROOF: renaming one pattern to a title no case prints reddens the check and names the gate, the row and the pattern.

rows.name: d1-anchored-surface
rows.note: NM-D1 SHIPPED. `presenter.presentAnchored(panel, opts)` places a surface against a SOURCE VIEW'S screen rect (`controller.screenRectOf`) instead of a parent corner, and it OWNS almost nothing: the stack, focus scope, input context, layering band, tap-away catcher and dismissal outcome are reached by delegating straight to `present`/`presentModal`, so every PresentOpts key works unchanged and `opts.modal = true` is the whole difference between a callout and a menu. TWO NEW MODULES, and the split is the point. `src/layout/anchor_placement.luau` is the PURE decision — plain numbers in, a plain placement out, no env/signals/theme/engine, the `popup_button.resolvePresentation` shape — and it is what let BOTH hand-rolled precedents be migrated rather than forked: the presenter's disclosure plate (`clampDisclosure`) and `row_actions.computeMenuAnchor` now ask the same function. Migrating the plate FIXED a latent defect in it: it flipped whenever below did not fit, INCLUDING when above did not fit either, which is the 'worse place' row_actions' own ruling 4 forbids — one rule, encoded once, and the older copy was the wrong one. `src/present/anchored.luau` is the surface: the Screen/Anchor wrapper, the window-space offsets, and the tail. THE TAIL IS A 45°-ROTATED `UI.Box`, NOT A `UI.Path`: Path2D STROKES ONLY (no fill) and `path_shapes` exports arc/ring/needle with no triangle, so a stroked outline cannot read as the solid panel-coloured wedge the f1 plate has. Declared BEFORE the panel, so the renderer's document-order z walk paints it behind and the overlapping half is covered; it wears the panel's own `surface` role, so a theme swap moves both. It EATS ITS OWN GAP (a square of side s protrudes s*sqrt(2)/2), or it would be drawn over the control it points at. FOLLOWING A MOVING SOURCE ADDED NO WATCHER: `sync()` rides `refreshBody` (the cadence a real scroll already drives `syncGeometry` at) and `tickBody` (the cadence the disclosure clamp already rides, which is what catches a text measure landing after mount), and writes nothing while nothing moved. `rootPolicy` is REFUSED unless it is edgeToEdge — the offsets are window space, and an inset root would silently re-base every one of them by the safe-area inset. The fixture is f1-avatar-editor.jpeg reproduced at 390x844: anchored under a top-right + button, arrow UP at it, body SHIFTED LEFT (a centred 260px plate under a button centred at x=368 would end 108px off screen). WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: no gesture trigger exists yet (long-press, right-click and hover-dwell are D2/D3a and are PENDING_PHYSICAL under `physical-and-human-rows`), no construct consumes the seam in a shipped screen yet (Menu/help/Callout are the next three deliverables, and RascalRally's rider PROVES it declares none — restraint measured off the source, not inferred), and no Studio capture was taken: this is E1 evidence for a placement decision that is pure arithmetic plus a headless mount.

rows.name: d2-menu
rows.note: NM-D2 SHIPPED. `Facet.newMenu` is a freestanding ACTION menu attachable to ANY blueprint — the returned `blueprint` IS the caller's own trigger node carrying an input contribution, so nothing is wrapped and no layout moves. Items are VERBS (`{ id, label, icon?, role?, enabled?, onSelect }`) plus a divider and a submenu item; `popup_button.Option` (`{ id, label }`, and a `value` that is a `Signal<string>`) cannot express one, which is why this is a second control rather than a property. THE ROW RECIPE WAS EXTRACTED, NOT AUTHORED (director call §5): `src/controls/menu_recipe.luau` holds the one row body and the one presentation rule, and `newMenu`, `newPopupButton` and `newRowActions`' action menu all render from it — `popup_button.resolvePresentation` is now an ALIAS ASSIGNMENT, which is why this row greps for the name and AGAINST a second `function` definition of it, and why neither row_actions nor popup_button still BUILDS a `compactLabel` prop of its own — both call `menuRecipe.row`, which is what the row greps here assert. The leaf row's props are byte-identical because two shipped cases pin them: the menu-flip prediction is exact only while MenuRows stays a padding-free VStack of fixed-height rows, and the large-text case reads `controller.textAt(<row path>)` for the row's own label — both are grepped here, which is the proof the migration is behaviour-neutral. SUBMENUS ARE STRUCTURALLY UNBOUNDED AND DIAGNOSED AT DEPTH >= 2 (director ruling: nothing caps the depth, the interface guidance advises one level; an earlier draft capped at 2 and was wrong in both directions), and the row asserts BOTH halves plus the silence at one level — a diagnostic that always fires is not advice. TOUCH DOES NOT NEST: under `sheet` a submenu REPLACES the panel's contents and grows a Back row (`dump().surfaces` is 1 at any depth), under `menu` it stacks anchored to its PARENT ROW with edge=trailing; one branch, resolved from space and live input class, never a device name. A MENU WHOSE EVERY ITEM IS DISABLED STILL OPENS (the standing rule), and the mutation that counts enabled items before presenting reddens two cases. THE LONG-PRESS COLLISION WAS MEASURED AND DECIDED THE OTHER WAY FROM THE BRIEF: the disclosure plate KEEPS the gesture, because it is the only touch route to a truncated label's full value (`reveal` is opt-in, UI.Text-only, one-at-a-time and absent under reduced motion; a disclosing Toggle label or Table cell has no marquee even in principle; and `text_audit.clippedEssential` checks the DECLARATION, never the reachability, so the removal would have been invisible). `newMenu` carves out only its own trigger subtree via `contribution.contextTriggers` -> `handle.contextTriggerOwns` -> an early return in `_discloseLongPress`, and a menu declared without a touch trigger claims nothing. All three directions are pinned: the plate still fires outside a trigger, it yields inside one, and a source sweep fails the day a third file in src/ learns the word — which is the alarm D3a's `help` has to clear. THE TRIGGER HALF CONSUMES WHAT ALREADY SHIPPED (the comparison document §5.2's own conclusion: "the adaptation layer is built, tested, and exported, and nothing consumes it as a trigger"): long-press is read off `adapter.setTouchGestureHandlers`, never re-recognized. The one channel that did NOT exist is the pointer's secondary button — `Button`'s Activated fires for the primary button and touch only — so `setSecondaryActivate` is a new OPTIONAL capability, and both reach a control through one nilable renderer seam so an adapter missing either degrades by name. ELEVEN MUTATIONS WERE RUN AND EVERY ONE WAS SEEN TO FAIL, including the two that matter most: unwiring the disclosure's long-press half reddens `a pointer world wires hover…` in text_disclosure.spec (the a11y alarm), and a new src/ file mentioning longPress reddens the source sweep. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: no gesture here is proved on hardware. Studio cannot synthesize a real touch or gamepad input class and an injected pointer event arrives as Touch rather than MouseButton2, so long-press, right-click and the gamepad trigger are all PENDING_PHYSICAL (NM-X1, NM-X2) — what is proved is the routing and the decisions, through the real adapter seams.

rows.name: d3a-help
rows.note: NM-D3a SHIPPED, and it is a PROP plus a CHECK rather than a construct. `UI.Button{ help = "…" }` (also legal on `Text`, `Toggle` and `TextField`) is one sentence about what a view DOES, PULLED by the player: pointer hover after the same 0.45 s dwell the disclosure plate uses, keyboard/gamepad on focus, immediately. NOTHING ON TOUCH, AND THAT IS THE SPECIFICATION — help is a desktop help tag plus an accessibility hint, and a tooltip is pointer-hover-only, and there is no touch trigger and NO LONG-PRESS BINDING ANYWHERE IN THAT API. Neither is there one here: D2 measured the collision and left touch long-press with the full-value disclosure plate — the only touch route to a truncated label's own value — and the renderer's zone wiring here takes the HOVER HALF ONLY, proved at the ADAPTER SEAM in BOTH repos rather than from source, while D2's own source sweep still fails if a third file in src/ learns the word. THE CONSEQUENCE IS A RULE, AND THE RULE IS MECHANICAL: because a touch player never sees it, `help` may never be the only route to something a player needs, so `text_audit.helpRoutes` ships with it and asks TWO questions rather than one. `helpOnlyRoute` reports a help string the screen paints nowhere else and IS waivable through `opts.convenience`; `helpNoRoute` reports help that NO live gesture reaches and is NOT — which is exactly the half `clippedEssential` structurally cannot do, because it accepts the DECLARATION `disclose = true` and never asks whether the plate is still reachable (D2's own finding, and the reason removing that binding would have been invisible). The routes are MEASURED, not declared: `presenter.helpDeclarations()` walks the mounted tree and reads `hover` off the LIVE pointer class as the renderer wired it and `focus` off `focus_map`'s own FOCUSABLE set, so the same fixture answers differently in a pure-touch session. THE PLATE IS CHROME, NOT A SURFACE, and that turned out to be structural rather than a setting: a presented surface pushes a focus scope even when it holds nothing focusable, and a scope with no members is still the TOP one — measured, the first arrow press after a plate appeared had nowhere to go and the ring on the described control went nil. So D1's seam gained a `chrome` mode (a hand-mounted controller: no stack, no scope, no input context, and the same solver, tail, safe box and follow cadence), which writes down once the pattern the disclosure plate and the toast strip already had rather than hand-rolling a fourth. NO ARROW TAIL, deliberately — a help tag has none, and the tail is what tells the app-pushed coach mark apart. A TRUNCATED `disclose` LABEL OUTRANKS IT on the same engagement, because a player who cannot read the label needs the value before the convenience, and the two are never both on screen. ONE SHIPPED FRAMEWORK BEHAVIOUR CHANGED BESIDE IT: `focus_graph.pushScope` no longer blanks the ring for a NON-TRAPPING scope that asked for `initialFocus = "none"`; a TRAP still does, and both directions are pinned in the Rascal Rally rider because every Sponsor surface this game presents goes through that call. EIGHT MUTATIONS, EVERY ONE SEEN TO FAIL: help appearing on touch, help binding long-press, the plate presented as a surface instead of chrome, the dwell firing instantly, the disclosure plate no longer outranking it, the waiver silencing `helpNoRoute`, truncated text counting as spoken, and the pushScope revert — two of them re-run against the game suite. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: everything here is E1. Studio cannot synthesize a real pointer class and an injected event arrives as Touch, so whether 0.45 s FEELS like a decision on a real mouse, and whether a pad player ever finds the plate, are physical-device rows (`physical-and-human-rows`). And Facet has no accessibility-hint channel, so the OTHER half of help — the screen-reader hint — has no analogue here and is not claimed.

rows.name: d3b-callout
rows.note: NM-D3b SHIPPED. `Facet.newCallout` is the APP-PUSHED coach mark, not a tooltip — and the split is the deliverable: a tooltip is PULLED by the player and invisible on touch (`help`, D3a, a prop), while this is raised from rules, appears on every input class and carries D1's arrow tail. It reproduces the reference `f1` plate: below a top-right `+`, body SHIFTED LEFT to stay on screen, arrow still over the button. CONTENT IS A BLUEPRINT, not a string, because that plate is styled and holds two lines. ELIGIBILITY is the coach-mark construct's actual contribution and every rule is a READ of caller state — `seen` (once per player), `sessions` + `afterSessions`, `featureUsed` — and INVALIDATION is permanent: feature used, player dismissed, or explicit, after which nothing in the session brings it back. PERSISTENCE IS THE CALLER'S AND THE BOUNDARY IS ENFORCED AT AUTHORING TIME: `onRetire(reason)` is REQUIRED, the framework writes nothing, and both suites carry the case that fails the day one starts — which for this game would mean writing into a live profile. AT MOST ONE ON SCREEN is `toast_schedule` configured `maxVisible = 1` rather than a second scheduler, so priority ordering, the queue cap and the read floor priority may never truncate all arrive with it; the one configuration choice worth stating is that a coach mark WAITS FOR THE PLAYER, so its duration is a finite number no session reaches rather than `math.huge`, which that model's own isFinite guard would silently replace with the four-second toast default. IT NEVER BLOCKS, and every half of that is DRIVEN rather than asserted: presenting one does not move the focus ring, the base screen keeps its own focus order, a tap on the pointed-at control still ACTIVATES IT (counted, because a swallowed tap looks identical from outside) and leaves the plate standing — the reference behaviour, where the mark is visible and unchanged across a whole clip while the player works beneath it — and a tap in empty space retires it through the presenter's own catcher. IT CARRIES ITS OWN WAY OUT ON ALL FOUR CLASSES: pointer and touch tap the plate's `Dismiss` row (44px floor asserted), keyboard and gamepad reach that row with ONE arrow press and press Return / ButtonA, and the ring returns afterwards. The standing warning ships VERBATIM in api.md and a spec holds the document to it. THE SHOWCASE SCENARIO is `examples/gallery/scenarios/callout`, registered in the scenario ORDER, in `demo_picker.DEMOS` and in the overflow sweep: the f1 plate under a top-right `+`, a press counter beneath it that IS the non-blocking claim on screen rather than in a document, a second coach mark that makes the queue something a player can see, and two readouts that are the persistence boundary — what the framework reported, and what that fixture then chose to save. SIX MUTATIONS, EVERY ONE SEEN TO FAIL: a modal presentation, `maxVisible = 2`, a retired callout presenting again, the framework writing `seen` itself, `onRetire` made optional, and the queue ignoring the surface its plate points at — plus two more against the game suite. ONE MUTATION DID NOT BITE AND IS RECORDED WITH ITS REASON, in the evidence file and in a comment beside the declaration: flipping the tap-away catcher to `consume = true` changes nothing observable, because `catchers.onPopupCatcherTap` dismisses and returns either way (an empty-space tap pressed no rendered node, so there is nothing to forward) and the presenter's rendered-sibling path iterates the contributions of the handle owning the TAPPED node, which is the screen underneath rather than this surface. The declaration stays because it is the true statement about what this surface must never swallow, not because a test caught it. THE RETIREMENT MUTATION ALSO FOUND A HOLE IN THIS STAGE'S OWN SPEC and it was closed: `eligible()` ignoring `retired` reddened nothing, because the case that covered it also declared `featureUsed`, which refused for a different reason — there is now a case with neither. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: everything is E1. Nothing here has been seen on a device — whether the wedge reads under a real theme (D1's own NM-D1-12, which this is the first construct to put on screen), whether the plate sits comfortably under a thumb, and whether a player finds the `Dismiss` row are all physical rows. And no Rascal Rally surface adopts it: the rider is a framework-presence check plus a tripwire, and that tripwire had to pin a FILE SET rather than a zero because this game already spells `help` for something else entirely — the Sponsor card FAMILY, across thirteen files. CALL SWAPPED 2026-08-22 (purity-sweep review MED-1): `lune run tools/lune/check_docs` builds the module and exits 0 whatever the documents say — measured in a content-pinned copy at 0 bytes of output and exit 0 against a tree whose api.md had dropped a public export, where `check_docs_cli` exits 1 and names it. The row now calls the cli form.

rows.name: d4-sliding-indicator
rows.note: NM-D4, the substrate D5 and D6 both consume — so its public SHAPE mattered more than its first consumer, and the director settled that shape mid-stage: THE SLIDING INDICATOR IS A PROPERTY, NOT A CONSTRUCT. `src/controls/selection_indicator.luau` is INTERNAL — no `src/init.luau` export (the gate greps for its absence), no api.md heading of its own, and no dump schema of its own; its live state rides `picker.dump().indicator`, and its registry row names `newPicker` the way `VirtualWindow` and `RowActionsTrays` already name the control they serve. The public surface is `newPicker`'s `indicator = "none" (default) | "underline" | "pill"` plus `axis`, and D5's TabView will carry the same pair. `indicator defaults to none: the pre-D4 control is byte-identical` is the row that makes the addition free for every existing caller. The seam itself is a LAYOUT SEAM rather than a control or a modifier: it owns no value, takes no input and is never a focus stop, while the constitution's positional-scalar modifier family is closed (§16 E-18). It is told nothing about its host — `content` (any strip blueprint), `segments` ({value, id} pairs) and `selected` (the owner's Readable, never written) — and resolves each child's SOLVED RECT by id at run time, which is why one seam serves a horizontal tab strip, a horizontal pill and a VERTICAL pill without either consumer subclassing it. THE TRANSITION IS BETWEEN TWO RECTS, NEVER TWO INDICES: segments stop being equal-width the moment their labels differ (r2's `For you` vs `Charts`) and again under a 1.4x pseudo-localization, so an index interpolation would put the bar under nothing for the whole flight and land it at the wrong width. Four scalar springs carry x, y, w and h — `object` (ζ 1.0, 0.28 s), the class small flying things already use — built lazily from the presenter's own clock through `bindMotion`, exactly row_actions' shipped shape, with an instant placement as the supported no-clock degradation. GEOMETRY ARRIVES ON THE ARRANGE CADENCE AND IS COMPARED BY VALUE AT TWO STAGES, and they fail DIFFERENTLY, which is why both are pinned: `syncGeometry` is fed on every solve AND every refresh with a fresh flat table, so an identity-compared intake costs a derivation per idle refresh (`repeated geometry feeds with UNCHANGED rects cost nothing`, counted in intake notifications rather than inferred), while an identity-compared TARGET re-places — and therefore SNAPS — the bar mid-slide every time anything else on the surface re-solves (`a geometry change that does not move the bar cannot interrupt a flight in progress`, driven by growing a sibling ABOVE the strip so every fed rect moves and the relative one does not). The comparator is renderer.luau:2778-2800's `sameGeometryValue` field for field, nested-table REFUSAL included: a rebuilt-outer/reused-inner shape compared by identity reports a false `unchanged`, which is a MISSED update and not a spare one. `rectOf`, NOT `screenRectOf`: the indicator lives in the same parent as the strip, so subtracting two raw host-space rects cancels every shift both share — screen space would apply D5's horizontal ScrollView offset twice. REDUCED MOTION SNAPS WITH NO BRANCH IN THIS MODULE: a `clock:spring` value is decorative, and the motion authority's I-4 invariant already places a decorative `setTarget` at its terminus on the same frame, so the fact is read where it already was rather than re-plumbed. The proof COUNTS FRAMES — one rect write then twenty ticks of silence, at the seam AND through the picker property — paired with `full motion spends MANY frames on the same change`, without which `never animate` would satisfy it. WRAPPING IS NOT FREE, and the game rider found the cost first: a `fill` strip inside a content-sized wrapper has nothing to fill and solved to ZERO width, so the wrapper inherits the strip's own dimension and `wrapping does not collapse a .fill. strip` compares the indicated control against the plain one rather than against a number somebody chose. TURNING IT ON CHANGES WHAT THE OPTIONS PAINT, deliberately: they drop the `selected` style tag and go `surface = plain`, because a tag AND a chip is the same statement twice and an opaque Button would paint OVER the chip meant to sit behind its label. The options also move one level deeper, so `selection still works at the deeper path` is the case that proves the move did not quietly break the control it decorates. NEVER A TAB STOP, asserted rather than assumed, at the seam and at the picker: the two classes it mounts (Anchor, Box) are outside focus_map's FOCUSABLE set and the layer is declared FIRST inside the ZStack, so it paints BEHIND the strip and cannot take a gesture from a segment (ZIndexBehavior is Sibling; a GuiButton sinks input). LOCALIZATION-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by care — the bar is a function of the solved rect — and swept anyway at 4 preferences x 2 reference themes with NO declared clip gap (`LT8-CTL Picker-indicator`). ONE CHECKER CHANGE, GUARDED: `check_registration` read `contribution.attach` as `interactive`, which was right for every control that had ever attached one, but this bundle is pure INTAKE (syncGeometry + bindMotion) and advertises no verb on any class; `CONTRIBUTION_INTAKE_ONLY` is the explicit exemption in the shape INTERACTIVE_ACTION_EXCEPT already uses, and a listed module that mentions any verb-bearing field loses it immediately. TWELVE MUTATIONS WERE RUN AGAINST THE SHIPPED SOURCE AND ALL TWELVE BIT (the ledger is in the evidence file), including the four that matter most: identity-comparing either guard, aiming the springs by snapping, and dropping the wrapper's declared width. RASCAL RALLY RIDES ALONG WITH NO PRODUCTION EDIT, audited rather than assumed — the game builds no picker at all — so the rider is a framework-presence check, a TRIPWIRE that fails the day any src/ file builds one, and a positive control driven against the guarantee this game would notice first: reduced motion, counted in frames. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: everything here is E1. No device and no human evidence exists yet — whether a 4px bar reads under a finger, whether the chip's contrast survives a themed package, and whether the flight FEELS like one object moving are NM-4.9, owed by D5/D6 as the first consumers to reach a device. Nothing here measures the cost of a size change: width/height carry `dirty = measure`, so a slide between UNEQUAL segments re-measures once per animated frame (a picker's options are equal-weight fills, so the shipped consumer slides arrange-only) and no benchmark was run against the unequal case. And the D6 work this stage did NOT do is still D6's: `Option` gains no `icon` here, and no shipped surface was migrated onto the property.

rows.name: d5-tabview
rows.note: NM-D5 SHIPPED. `Facet.newTabView` — the construct `adaptive.navPlacement` had been waiting for since 2026-08-09, while all five reference apps built the bar by hand. THE STRIP IS `newPicker` (director call, additive-vs-net-new.md §6): same option row, same icons, same 44px floor, same D4 sliding indicator, same authoring lints, and `dump().strip` is that control's own dump nested rather than paraphrased. Everything the strip needed landed THERE as a property or a widening — `sizing` (a `fill` strip CANNOT overflow, so an autoscroll built on the default tests nothing), a reactive `axis` (a placement flip is a re-solve, not a rebuild), `Option.badge`, and a Readable `Option.label` — plus `api.segments`, because `controller.scrollToVisible` takes a mounted PATH and string arithmetic on "Opt1" is the assumption that breaks. THE NESTING RULE, stated in source: THE APP-LEVEL PLACEMENT BELONGS TO THE OUTERMOST TABVIEW, and it is decidable without asking the caller because `content` is a FACTORY this control invokes — a TabView built during that invocation is inside one (`dump().placementSource` reports policy/declared/nested). The other two things two live TabViews could fight over are never CLAIMED: no focus scope, no `back()` stack, because a TabView is a layout construct and not a presentation. EVICTION IS `UI.When`'S OWN BRANCH SCOPE, not a second mechanism, so the escape hatch is ownership rather than a `retain` flag — and the neutrality spec takes its baseline AFTER one warm-up cycle, because the D4 indicator builds its four springs lazily and a baseline before the first switch counts that as a leak. THE BRIEF NAMED THE WRONG AUTOSCROLL API and this row verified it: `src/input/autoscroll.luau` is a drag-to-edge pointer-proximity model with vertical bands only; `controller.scrollToVisible` IS `solver.keepVisibleOffset` applied to a mounted rect, and a keyboard/gamepad move is ALREADY revealed by the presenter, so only a selection change that did not move focus is handled here. THREE SHIPPED DEFECTS FOUND: the selection indicator learned its mounted paths exactly once (a re-homed strip froze its bar); a `space.xs` underline cannot wear a themed control's chrome (87 findings across the theme matrix — it paints with `tint` now, p4_foyer's own idiom); and `focus_map` matched `HStack` alone in THREE places, so every segmented picker in the framework navigated VERTICALLY on a pad while Right walked out of the control. That last rule is BOUNDED — a run is a node no child of which holds more than one focusable — because an `AdaptiveStack` is also how a construct flips a whole screen, and Rascal Rally's only one is exactly that shape. p4_foyer is MIGRATED (155 lines of nav assembly deleted: four hand-built bars, four placement memos, three copies of the wing list, a hand-rolled active bar, a ViewThatFits ladder and a rail width), which closed one theme-ledger row outright. Everything here is E1: the gamepad shoulders are PENDING_PHYSICAL by construction, no Studio canary was run, and p4's centred top/compact cluster is now leading-aligned — a measured trade (a `fill` child inside a horizontal ScrollView resolves to the CONTENT width, and a ViewThatFits ladder mounts the strip twice), stated in the file and in the evidence rather than hidden. RE-PINNED 2026-08-22: the `src/init.luau` clause read `newTabView = require`, which ADR-0037 (`8691380`) retired when it hoisted every control require to the top of the file and added the `Facet.Controls` namespace. It now pins four literals instead of one — the require, the module path, the compatible `newTabView` alias and the typed `Controls.TabView` entry — so the wrong-builder wiring ADR-0037 calls the real hazard is visible from here too. NO NESTED QUOTES IN A PIN, EVER: `"` is a legal Lua escape, so the shell receives a BARE quote and concatenates, and `require("@self/x")` reaches grep as the needle `require(@self/x)`, which matches nothing while looking perfectly deliberate.

rows.name: d6-segmented
rows.note: NM-D6 SHIPPED, and it is PROPERTIES-ONLY by director call (artifacts/navigation-and-menus/additive-vs-net-new.md §1): no new construct, no new module, three keys on a control that already existed. THE ONE THING THAT IS NOT ADDITIVE IS THE DEFAULT, and it is the point of the stage: `indicator` now spells `automatic` and RESOLVES TO THE PILL unless the caller declared `presentation = "inline"`. D4 shipped `"none"` so nothing on screen moved, which was right for a stage whose job was the mechanism and wrong to leave — a mechanism nobody consumes by default is an unproven mechanism, and every reference screenshot of a segmented control (r3, f1's top pill, f1's left rail) draws a chip. The rule deliberately reaches `presentation = "automatic"`, which is what most callers write; a default that only reached a DECLARED `segmented` would have changed 7 of 15 callers instead of 14 of 15. AN ADAPTIVE PICKER THAT FLIPS INTO ITS STACKED FORM CARRIES ITS CHIP DOWN WITH IT — one selection paint re-solved rather than two paintings swapping, which is what the A-AL2 rule already promises for everything else about this control, and what avoids a reactive `surface` toggle whose inactive value has no honest answer (an undeclared Button surface is not `control`, and a nil write reaches the real adapter as the string "nil"). `indicator = "none"` is the documented escape hatch and is byte-identical to the pre-D4 control — D4's own case now asks for it by name, re-pointed in this commit rather than three stages later. THE FULL CALLER SURVEY IS 15, ONE PINNED: `tools/lune/_theme_baseline.luau`'s `control-vocabulary` picker is the frozen input `check_flat_baseline` compares node-for-node against the stored 0.6.0 render, and that comparison IS the flat-theme byte-compatibility claim (ADR-0020 R9), so letting the new default in would have re-pinned the framework claim to make a paint change quiet — the exact failure that checker's own header warns about. Every other caller (7 declared `segmented`: time_curves, sorted_entries, text_degrade, with_animation, flow_wrap, settings_panel, showcase_chrome; 7 `automatic` that resolve segmented: adaptive_controls, p2 gallery x2, p2 topfive, p2 ledger, p5 wardrobe x2) took the chip with no source edit and no spec change beyond the option paths moving one level deeper. ICONS FOLLOW THE SHIPPED RULING RATHER THAN A SECOND ONE. `Option.icon` is a semantic NAME riding `compactLabel` (Button.icon is circle-only; a segment is a rectangle), and `iconOnly` picks which of the two 2026-08-12 device-round readings applies to the GROUP: without it the segment keeps its word and degrades to the glyph (row_actions.luau:1774, the menu row — `the ladder really RUNS` proves the degrade at 200px so `the word survives` cannot be satisfied by never declaring the icon at all), with it `prefer = true` makes the glyph what every segment wears at every width (row_actions_trays.luau:346, the tray, and f1). It is a group call because a per-segment verdict is how one plate wears a glyph while its neighbour wears a word. THREE AUTHORING RULES REFUSE AT CONSTRUCTION rather than on a screen: every option needs a non-empty `label` (it is the semantic name, it is what `semanticText` announces, and `check_registration` cannot see an unreadable glyph), a group carries icons on ALL options or none, and `iconOnly` with no icons is refused instead of ignored. THE VERTICAL PILL AND THE INLINE ROW LIST ARE TWO FACTS, NOT ONE, because both stack along y and both report `axis = "y"`: `verticalPill` is computed separately, drives the container, and is reported by `dump()` so a bug report about width has a field to name. The rail is content-sized with a 44px FLOOR and that floor is load-bearing rather than defensive — an icon-only rail's natural width is a glyph, measured at 36px, under the target on both axes — and the floor rides `targetSizes.minimum`, not a number. The width is a MEMO on all three nodes (root, wrapper, option stack) because a live space change that stacks the control must give the offer back; a build-time answer leaves a 44px column where a full-width row list belongs, which `flipping OUT of segmented gives the offer back` fails on. DUMP STAYS /1, decided rather than defaulted: D6 only ADDS fields (`verticalPill`, `requestedIndicator`, `iconOnly`, `iconCount`, `selectedIcon`), every shipped field keeps its name, type and meaning, and a schema string exists to warn about an INCOMPATIBLE shape. DOCS SAY THE TAB-BAR THING IN BOTH PLACES: api.md's newPicker and the comparison document's Picker row both state that a segmented picker used as a tab bar IS TabView, which owns the content subtree, the screen-restructuring placement and nesting, and which COMPOSES this strip — the source header says so too, so D5 finds the instruction where it will be standing. THIRTEEN MUTATIONS WERE RUN AGAINST THE SHIPPED SOURCE; TWELVE BIT AND THE THIRTEENTH IS RECORDED AS NOT BITING, with the reason, in the evidence file and in a comment beside the declaration it tests (the indicator wrapper's width is pinned twice over on the rail path, so no mutation of it alone moves a solved rect; it is kept because it is the true statement, not because a test caught it). RASCAL RALLY CAUGHT THE FLIP FIRST: its D4 rider asserted the old default and went red on the framework change before any D6 spec existed, which is the rider doing exactly the job the lockstep rule gives it. There is still NO production edit — the game builds no picker anywhere under src/, read off the source by the tripwire every run — so the consumer work is the D4 rider corrected plus a new D6 rider that drives icons, the lint, the rail's 44px floor on both axes and the new default through THIS package's framework require. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: everything here is E1. No device and no human evidence — whether an icon-only 44px rail is comfortable under a thumb, whether the chip's contrast survives a themed package, and whether the degrade-to-glyph boundary lands where a designer would put it are NM-4.9/E3-E5 rows, still owed and now owed by a CONSUMED mechanism rather than an unconsumed one. No example migrated to icons or to the vertical rail: both ship with spec consumers only, which is the honest state and the one thing a device pass should be pointed at first. THE ROW WAS SYNTACTICALLY DEAD FOR A DAY, and both of its guardians reported green. `1482571` (a commit about file locations) deleted the closing quote of the `all options in a group, or none of them` needle and changed nothing else on the line; bash then refused the WHOLE run string with `unexpected EOF`, so the twenty-two clauses after it — three picker source pins, two api.md pins, the parity pin, the device-name scan, the theme-baseline pin, `check_docs`, `check_theme_drift_cli`, `check_source_size` and ALL EIGHT Rascal Rally suite greps — stopped running on 2026-08-21. `check_gate_pins` could not see it (every needle it could parse matched) and `check_manifest_integrity` could not either (every pattern was anchored and matching): a row can be DEAD while both guards are green. Restored 2026-08-22, whereupon the entire tail passed unchanged — nothing behind the typo had drifted. `tools/check_gate_pins.py` now parses every run string with `bash -n`, and the replanted typo is its mutation. CALL SWAPPED 2026-08-22 (purity-sweep review MED-1), same measurement as d3b-callout: the bare `check_docs` module form cannot fail, the `_cli` form can, and this row now calls the one that can.

rows.name: d7-elision-discloses
rows.note: NM-D7 SHIPPED. THE PRINCIPLE: adaptation may change how much of something is shown, and what it costs to reach it; it may not change whether it can be reached at all. The rank ladder was NOT missing and NOT broken — ADR-0025's rank/forms/floor/mayDrop does exactly what it is told. What it lacked was any notion of WHERE the elided content went, so from the player's side 'step down' and 'delete' were one operation. Measured on the showcase before any edit: 39 elided-or-dropped occurrences across nine viewports x two URL-bar states, EVERY ONE a dead end (artifacts/navigation-and-menus/d7-hud-baseline.md). SHIPPED: `recover` as a closed spec on UI.Region ('none' | 'self' | 'overflow'), REQUIRED with more than one form and REFUSED with one — required rather than defaulted because silence is not consent, and 51 declarations were migrated by reading their forms rather than by defaulting (18 showcase/reference, 15 suite, 18 RascalRally). The two halves live in DIFFERENT modules and that is a measurement: `forms` reaching the solver is the count of MOUNTED forms and a `UI.When`-gated form comes and goes, so the pure normalizer owns 'required' and UI.Region owns 'refused'. `elided` beside `dropped`, and `Resolution.unshown` — the SEAM an overflow surface is populated from, in declaration order, with a dropped region's route always 'overflow' whatever its recover said. A 'self' route is checked against EVERY form below the richest, not only the last: the ladder can stop at any rung. THE HOST FINDING, which the brief's own D7.3 assumption got wrong: the '...' was not merely non-rank-1, it lived in a FORM the ladder never chose, so it was Visible=false at every swept viewport — the round strip had been showing two of its three buttons for the fixture's whole life. It is now ONE wrapped form, so it cannot elide (recover is refused on a one-form region) and cannot drop. THE SCORES ARE THE CASE NO RE-RANK COULD FIX: the Clock is in the CENTRE lane and the fps readout in the RIGHT one, and rule 3 spends only the currency of the lane that does not fit — so fps goes 7->9 and the scoreboard gets the disclosure route instead. URL BAR RE-MEASURED against a real browser (Chrome 151, a local page reporting outerHeight-innerHeight: 143px normal window, 67px popup with a location bar and no tab strip). The fixture models the 67 because a tab strip does not APPEAR; 200 was three times it, and the drawn bar was 733x158 = 42% of a 749x380 viewport. The second job is now a theme metric, not a constant. THE BASELINE'S 'FOURTH FAILURE CLASS' IS REFUTED WITH ARITHMETIC: 'Round 3 · Capture @(416,-37)' is not painted above the viewport — a Facet ScreenGui renders IgnoreGuiInset=true and AbsolutePosition is reported in the INSET-SUBTRACTED space, so window y 21 reads back as 21-58; the same capture reports three hidden nodes at y=-58, which is the origin proving its own offset, and the x centres agree exactly (456.5 both ways). Booked as a lesson addendum plus a regression at the baseline's own viewport. GuiObject A/B against the pre-D7 tree read out of HEAD with only `recover` props added: 144 -> 138 nodes, 88 -> 86 engine-backed, and the sink costs ZERO while closed. 14 mutations, 14 bite — two of them only after the tests were fixed: M6 ran at a height where the dropped region had one form, M8 at a height where the 'none' region had not stepped. RESIDUAL, booked not closed: `recover = overflow` says the screen OWES a route and does not prove one exists; the D7.6 sweep proves it for the HUD showcase, while the composition scenario, p2_cartwheel's workbench and RascalRally's results screen now declare it on surfaces that build no sink — the pre-existing gap, made visible in `unshown` instead of silent.

rows.name: d8-playlist-sort-resize
rows.note: NM-D8 SHIPPED. Sorting and per-column resize BOTH already shipped in `table.luau`, so this changed no framework behaviour — the only `src/` edits are two comments naming a file this row deletes. THE MEASUREMENT THE BRIEF MADE CONDITIONAL WAS REPEATED AND THE THIRD COLUMN SURVIVED IT. Instrument validated against the historical failure first: re-running the deleted third-FIXED-70px shape at 320x640 in EDIT MODE reproduces the file's own recorded numbers, Name cell 6px / text 0px with 3 `content box collapses to 0px on x` diagnostics. The third FILL column, same session, same viewport: Name 46/30, Artist 30/14, ZERO collapse diagnostics — so the brief's hypothesis (a fill column is a different animal from a fixed one) holds where it was posed, the row's SUBJECT keeps 30px of text where the fixed column left it none, and the price is the Artist cell at 14px of text at that one viewport in that one mode. Paid rather than hidden: both text columns carry `disclose = true` and both truncate to ONE line (lines 1/1, truncated) rather than wrapping into a row that cannot hold them, and every number is pinned in a case so it cannot drift. Two viewports up: 359x718 gives 69/53 and 46/30. THE THIRD COLUMN IS STRUCTURALLY REQUIRED, also measured: `resolveDim` turns any resized column into `{ type = fixed }`, so at 800x600 pinning Name to 200 in the TWO-column table painted 16..216 and 216..360 inside a cells region of 16..784 — 424px of dead space at the trailing edge — while three columns give 16..216 / 216..640 / 640..784 and fill it. A THIRD MEASURED FACT WORTH CARRYING: `minWidth` floors a RESIZE, not the LAYOUT (`resolveDim` applies it only to an override and to a `percent` band), so the declared 90/72 is the narrowest a PLAYER may drag to, not the narrowest the column is drawn; `{ type = minMax }` was tried instead and is wrong for the same reason `hug` was, header 90/70 against body 175/137. REORDER vs SORT: a manual reorder WINS and BAKES — the displayed order becomes the stored order and `sortOrder` goes nil — enforced at `reorder` and `moveToTop`, and deliberately NOT at `removeTrack`, because deleting a row from a sorted list leaves a sorted list. AND THE GUARD RUNS BEFORE THE BAKE, which is a defect this stage found in its own first draft: baking WRITES, so a Top naming a track already removed, or a drop carrying no keys, would have dropped the players sort on the way to doing nothing — a manual reorder clears the sort has to mean a reorder that actually happens. Both shapes are one case, and BOTH mutations (deleting either guard) redden it by name. The pre-existing reorder-under-filter REFUSAL is unchanged and is the opposite answer to a different question (a drop is ambiguous against hidden rows; it is not ambiguous against reordered ones). The chain is sort-over-source then filter-over-sorted, because filtering first leaves the full ordered list existing nowhere and both the bake and move-to-top need it. Ties break on the SOURCE INDEX (`table.sort` is not stable in Luau; two tracks share an artist so that is observable). RE-POINTED BEFORE DELETED, which is the named failure mode: 37 cases green on the tutorial and `hit_expander_overhang.spec.luau:43`s direct scenario require moved to the example, THEN the fixture went. `overflow_sweep`s RULE 4 list lost it too (the sweep list and the scenario registry are one set) and the header is still swept at every viewport x text preference by `example_readouts`, which is why this row greps that sweep. A BEHAVIOUR CHANGE THIS ROW OWNS: a sortable, resizable header is FOCUSABLE, so the playlist gained a focus stop — d-pad goes filter, header (ONE stop, Left/Right walks the columns), toolbar, rows; Tab goes Head-name, Head-artist, Head-rating, then the row. Three `examples_gallery` cases assert the new order explicitly rather than skipping it. AND THE THIRD STALE CLAIM, which the brief did not name and is the most public of them: the demo pickers `ex02` blurb read `Sortable, reorderable, filterable table` verbatim in the live FacetShowcaseAPI.list response, so the example advertised sorting to every device pass and every human reviewer while `grep -c sortOrder` on it returned 0. This row greps the corrected blurb. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: nothing here is a physical-touch claim — the divider is still 8px against a 44px floor (pinned again as grip8x28 under Touch) and whether a finger lands on it is the device row; and the 2026-08-14 live drives this work cites (the camera sinking the arrow keys, the 44px band per pixel) are carried forward as history rather than re-measured.

rows.name: rider-rascalrally-consumer
rows.note: THE LOCKSTEP RULE, AND WHY IT EARNED ITSELF TWICE THIS ROUND. Both Rascal Rally Rojo projects mount GameStudio/ui/Facet/src directly, so a Facet gate cannot pass while its consumer is stale, failing or unaudited. NO PRODUCTION GAME CODE CHANGED AND THAT IS THE CORRECT OUTCOME - nothing in the game builds a menu, a tab view, a callout or an anchored surface yet, and the rule explicitly forbids manufacturing an edit for a compatible internal change. What it requires instead is evidence the direct consumer still works, and that is eight new or extended contract specs driving each change through the GAME PACKAGE'S OWN framework require and presenter rather than through Facet's fixtures. THIS ROW CHECKS THE THREE THINGS THAT CAN ROT: the specs exist, they are REGISTERED in the game's tests/run.luau (an unregistered spec is a silent zero, and this round already found one registration omitted), and the game suite is green. TWICE THE RIDERS CAUGHT WHAT THE FRAMEWORK SUITE STRUCTURALLY COULD NOT: D4's found an indicated picker solving its options to 0px inside a CONTENT-SIZED wrapper - every framework fixture used fixed-width segments, so nothing headless could see it; and D6's went red at 3289/1 on the old-default assertion BEFORE any D6 spec existed, noticing the segmented default had moved before the framework's own coverage did. THE ONE BEHAVIOUR THESE RIDERS EXIST TO PROTECT: ten shipped Sponsor surfaces declare UI.Text{ disclose = true } and depend on the full-value plate still owning LONG-PRESS outside a menu trigger, which is why D2 scoped newMenu's claim to its own trigger subtree instead of taking the gesture outright. The grep for the rollback string is deliberate - game behaviour, content ownership and feature flags are unchanged, including the production Facet Sponsor default and the UseFacetSponsor = false legacy escape hatch. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: no Studio canary ran for this round's game surfaces, and the game consumes none of the new constructs yet, so this is a compatibility claim rather than an adoption one.

rows.name: physical-and-human-rows
rows.note: THIS ROW PASSES WHEN THE REVIEW PACKET IS READY, NOT WHEN THE DEVICE PASS IS DONE, and the distinction is the whole point. Execution contract §8: complete every automatable row, then produce ONE review build and ONE packet so the irreducible physical and human work is a single focused pass rather than a discovery exercise. The packet names fourteen rows — eight PENDING_PHYSICAL (long-press, right-click, hover-dwell, gamepad menu/tab paging, the playlist divider under a finger, the tail and chip under an ornate theme, the level-picker bars, and P8's haptics) and six PENDING_HUMAN (does the indicator read as one object moving, does a Callout read as help or as an ad, is an icon-only 44px rail comfortable, is the HUD disclosure route discoverable, the H4a paint-probe readout, and do the three segment modes read as one control) — each with the scenario, the exact action, the expected result, and the negative control. P8 IS THE ONE ROW WHOSE CHECK READS THE ANSWER VOCABULARY RATHER THAN ONLY THE HEADING, and the reason is the finding it came from: the director felt no haptics because the demo never constructed the adapter, and the repair is worthless if its report collapses to a boolean. So the three sentences a device can produce — Requested, This platform says no, Could not determine — are greped individually. Two of three passing is exactly the failure docs/lessons/capability-probes-must-be-tri-state.md is about, and this repository has shipped that collapse twice. THE SECOND HALF OF THIS CHECK IS THE HONEST ONE: it re-reads the acceptance ledger and fails if NM-X1/X2/X3 stop being PENDING_PHYSICAL or NM-X4/X5 stop being PENDING_HUMAN. A row cannot pass through a different, easier row, and the failure mode this guards is a future stage quietly relabelling a device row as PASS_AUTOMATED because a headless proxy went green. WHY NOTHING CHEAPER CLOSES THE TEN: Studio cannot synthesize a real touch or gamepad input class; an injected pointer event arrives as `Touch` rather than `MouseButton1`, so filtering it wrong manufactures a false positive that AGREES WITH YOU; a script-fired binding proves the downstream action path and never native arbitration; and no frame count can judge whether a spring reads as one object moving. releaseBlocking = false because the packet being ready is not a release claim — the ten rows themselves still block release, and they live in the ledger where a reader will see them. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: that any of the ten has been run. It claims only that a person could run all ten in one sitting without reading a line of source.

rows.note: Every two-or-more similarity finding consolidated under one narrow owner, or kept separate with the concrete recorded reason the plan demands. 'They may diverge later' is not enough. THE ROW'S OWN FIRST CLAUSE IS THE COMPLETENESS CHECK, and it is structural rather than a set of fixed greps: tools/check_reuse_ledger.py reads the audit's `### REUSE-n` headers — 125 of them — and requires reuse-ledger.md to disposition each exactly once, naming CONSOLIDATED, KEPT SEPARATE or DEFERRED. Four ways to fail, each a different mistake: MISSING, DUPLICATE, INVENTED and UNDISPOSED, and the selftest plants one of each in a scratch COPY of the ledger. This replaced five `grep -qF` sentence clauses that could not see the ledger carrying 16 of the 125 findings while opening with the sentence that it carried them all — the repository's own 'check that proves nothing' shape aimed at exactly the property RC-10 names. WHAT WAVE R5 CLOSED. Four dependency-free leaves own what a hundred private copies answered: `num` (isFinite x17, byte-identical, plus whole-pixel rounding), `paths` (the segment-aligned prefix test x7 — and TWO UNSAFE INLINE COPIES that were the live tap routing, so two presented screens named Menu and MenuBar routed each other's taps), `rect` (15+ bodies, four epsilons, two edge conventions) and `text_distance` (five bounded-Levenshtein matrices under two different suggest policies). REUSE-29 joined them in fix round 1: the hidden-roots filter had FOUR copies, not the three the audit counted, and `presenter.luau` imported the published owner and then shadowed it with a nested local. WHAT DID NOT MERGE IS THE POINT: rect ships BOTH point-in conventions under names that say what they do, because a tap exactly on a shared edge is inside for the modal-zone test and a miss for the tiled drop test and both are right; the epsilons stay arguments at the call sites, where they were decisions; and all five suggesters keep their own threshold WRITTEN OUT, because case-sensitive <=2 against case-folded max(2, floor(#name/3)) is a real user-visible disagreement nobody had ever decided. src/client/host.luau is the twelfth blessed client entry point and exists because the getting-started guide TAUGHT a Heartbeat refresh-only loop and never named tick: three of the four shipped game bootstraps and one in-repo example drove refresh alone, so their motion clocks never advanced and a toast never expired — invisible in every static instrument, because a frozen clock and a settled one look identical in a dump. Fix round 1 added the ninth bootstrap the census missed (docs/guide/08-without-rojo.md, the page an adopter without Rojo lands on), put the adapter and the input system on the host's undo stack so BOTH the failure path and a normal dispose release them, and moved the one-clock-one-driver claim onto the PRESENTER — motion_driver had asserted it since it shipped, but against a table private to itself, so a host plus a driver double-ticked in silence and every duration elapsed at double speed. tests/lib/world.luau took controller ruling R12's SCOPE: the substrate plus the spec files carrying the two incompatible five-tuple return orders (core, env, system, adapter, pres against core, env, adapter, system, pres — positions three and four swapped, the same five names on both sides, which Luau binds without a word).
