rows.note: InputContext/InputAction/InputBinding own semantic routing and lifetime; the complete legacy-service inventory is classified; every surviving legacy call has a current impossibility proof, one allowlisted adapter, tests, teardown, and a removal trigger; drift checks reject new direct legacy bindings; no old and new path fires together. WHAT WAVE R3 CLOSED. The inventory's 116 rows partition into five classes; only class 1 (semantic action routing) owed anything, and its five MUST-MIGRATE rows are now zero. InputAction:Fire is tagged DEPRECATED on the live class reference, so each fired action gained one Type=Scriptable child InputBinding created beside it in the consumer's server-side rig and the six client call sites Fire THAT (InputBinding:Fire respects the same deduplication rules as hardware input; Fire on an Automatic binding throws, which is why the binding is created explicitly). INPUT-105's hand-staged touch buttons — a GuiButton.InputBegan writing a pending true, a GLOBAL UserInputService.InputEnded identity-matching the release, a per-frame flush — became one InputBinding.UIButton each; the mobile drag-off-release bug that machinery worked around was fixed at the engine level 2026-04-07 (staff: the Released event will now fire), and the camera toggle already rode that seam. ARBITRATION. All four consumer InputContexts shipped with Priority and Sink at engine defaults, and the reference is explicit that contexts with the same priority will receive the input — DF-1..4 were four instances of that one omission (DF-6), each mitigated only by a STATE ASSUMPTION maintained elsewhere. Three bands, declared once and read by every construction site so the live numbers and the arbitrated numbers are the same numbers: modal 3000+Sink (the two overlays, each still deriving Enabled from its surface, because a sink that outlives its surface is a permanently deaf game), hud 2000 (the camera toggle), gameplay 1000 (the driving floor). DF-4 needed more than a number: its other consumer is a NATIVE GuiButton.Activated off GuiService.SelectedObject, not an InputContext, so the close is a no-op guard claiming ButtonA inside the sinking overlay — the idiom presenter.luau already uses for the keyboard jump (GameplayGuard on Space). Each pair is proved single-delivery in BOTH states through Facet's engine-free IAS model built from the shipped schema, and six mutations were confirmed to bite. THE FLAG. Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem now declared in all eight project files (3 of 8 before): both generated place projects, the reference-place project, and both consumer projects; all 15 Facet places rebuilt so the built .rbxl carries it — the served showcase project declared it while the built file a device opens did not. The module comment claiming the property is NOT script- OR ROJO-reflectable was HALF WRONG and that wrong half is why five project files went without it for months: rojo builds it fine with the pinned toolchain (re-proved this session against a negative control — a made-up property fails the build, this one does not). The script-read half stands, so every detector here stays behavioural. DF-9 answered with that: iasPlayerScriptsActive() reads the ARTIFACT of the flag (Player.InputContexts.CharacterContext/CameraContext/VehicleContext exist only under it) and disableLegacyControls() returns an explicit inert verdict plus a status where IAS already owns the player scripts, unchanged where it does not — with the order pinned, because an inert check running second would still pay the bounded PlayerModule wait. THE DRIFT GUARD. tools/check_input_authority.py refuses a new direct ContextActionService use or a new InputBegan/InputEnded/InputChanged subscription outside the allowlisted adapters, over src/, examples/ and the consumer's src/, on comment-stripped Luau through the lexer check_no_screen_key_bindings.py already ships (string CONTENTS stay visible — a service name inside a GetService call is the bypass being hunted). It is deliberately not narrowed to a receiver named UserInputService: an alias walks through that, and the per-node GuiObject.InputBegan form is the same class. THREE RULES, all biting: an unallowlisted flagged file fails; an ALLOWLISTED file with no flagged site fails (a stale exemption whose removal trigger has fired — InputBridge.luau earned that rule immediately, dropping off the hit list when the UIButton migration landed); and a NO_IAS_SURFACE verb whose witness token has vanished fails, so the impossibility ledger cannot become fiction. Eight allowlisted adapters each carry their inventory class, the platform text that makes them necessary NOW, and the event that retires them; six ledger verbs carry the same. The selftest plants into a scratch COPY of the real src/ tree rather than the working tree — the identical scan over identical contents, so the proof is the same one, while a concurrent reader never sees a planted file. WHAT IS STILL OWED, and it is engine-only: DF-7's PrimaryModifier-times-Sink interaction is UNMEASURED and no binding was changed for it (its own bare-PENDING row below); whether an IAS sink also starves the native Activated (DF-4's other half); and whether a Scriptable/UIButton binding relays to a SERVER-created action under Server Authority, which the platform docs do not walk through at all. All of it is booked in artifacts/release-candidate-review/input/studio-checklist.md with what to drive, what to read, and the predicted value.

rows.name: df7-modifier-sink-measured
rows.note: THE HIGHEST-VALUE OPEN INPUT QUESTION IN THE RELEASE CANDIDATE, and it is a MEASUREMENT, not a fix. row_actions.luau:213 binds Return with modifiers shift=true inside a priority-10000 sink=true context, while the base screen binds plain Return to Activate at 1500/3500 (presenter.luau:2251). The engine documents InputContext.Sink as operating BY KEYCODE — the lower priority contexts will not receive the input signal for Enum.KeyCode.E — and documents InputBinding.PrimaryModifier as gating whether a BINDING triggers its action. The two sentences do not compose, and nothing anywhere states whether a modifier narrows what its context SINKS. WAVE R3 MADE NO BINDING CHANGE, deliberately: both failure modes are silent and a change made without a reading would be a guess wearing a fix's clothes. The headless model (actions.luau modifierMatch plus deviceKey) filters modifier-mismatched bindings out of candidacy BEFORE the sink loop, which selects outcome (a) below — but that is a design decision recorded in a comment, not a measurement, and the model passing its own tests is not evidence about the engine. THE THREE POSSIBLE READINGS. (a) plain Return still activates a focused row and Shift+Return opens only the menu, so the sink is per-binding-candidate, the model is right, nothing to do. (b) plain Return NO LONGER activates, so the sink is per-KeyCode and Enter stops activating rows for as long as ANY row-actions context is alive: a silent regression on a verb users already have, visible only while a row is focused. (c) plain Return activates AND Shift+Return fires both RowActionsMenu and Activate, so the engine sinks only on match but still offers the unmodified sibling: a double-fire. THE FALLBACK for (b) and (c), spelled out so it is not re-invented under pressure: rebind the menu to a keyboard chord sharing NO KeyCode with Activate. ButtonX already covers the gamepad, so only the keyboard side moves, and ROW_KEYS.menu is one table in one file whose pinned site count in tools/check_no_screen_key_bindings.py moves with it. HOW IT IS MEASURED: a REAL keyboard, the showcase place, a Table with row actions mounted, four presses in a fixed order with a control reading first — artifacts/release-candidate-review/input/studio-checklist.md section 5. The reading goes verbatim into the evidence file, which today holds the question and an explicitly empty THE READING section. This row stays a bare PENDING until it holds a real one.

rows.name: maintainer-map-current
rows.note: docs/MAINTAINERS.md maps all nineteen production areas — covering every one of the 28 top-level entries under src/ — to responsibility, public seam, internal owner modules, allowed dependency direction, covering specs, Studio scenario, gate row and extension playbook, plus the where-does-it-belong answers for a control, primitive, layout, modifier, engine property, render target, input behavior, device fact, theme feature, example, scenario, test helper and checker. IT IS A MAP AND NOT A SECOND CATALOG: no property, default or return value appears in it, because those belong to docs/reference/api.md and the guide index's capability catalog, and it carries NO COUNT a person would have to maintain — not a spec count, not a control count, not the size of the blessed client list. THE POINT OF THE ROW IS THE DRIFT CHECK. tools/lune/check_maintainer_map.luau reads every fact back out of the place it came from: the area list from the src/ tree on disk (so a new area is unmapped the moment it lands), coverage from the require graph one hop out of each spec file, gate stages and rows from this manifest, dependency rules by name from check_boundary's own reported strings, scenario names from the scenario index, and every link from the filesystem — including the anchor, which must be a heading the target document really has. It also refuses a shipped docs/extending playbook the map never links, so a new extension path cannot arrive unmapped. Twelve obligations, printed by --list, and the twelfth is the one a rename would otherwise walk through: every Facet.<name> the PUBLIC SEAM column advertises is read out of the exported library table itself, the same source check_docs reads, because the seam column is the one a maintainer trusts most and an unverified column in a map whose whole claim is that every fact is checked would be its weak link. THE COUNTS ARE DERIVED AND THE MAP DOES NOT STATE THEM: --counts prints per-area covering-spec numbers from the same require graph, which is where the map sends a reader instead of writing a number down. Nineteen suite cases plant one fault each into an in-memory copy (a suite run writes nothing) and require each to be named; the --selftest form plants the same faults into a real copy in a scratch directory keyed per run, which is the scratch-copy discipline check_input_authority uses and the reason a concurrent reader never sees a planted file. WHAT THE MAP CORRECTED ON ITS WAY IN: docs/guide/02-architecture.md said ELEVEN blessed client modules and omitted client/host.luau, while check_boundary and api.md both carry twelve — a restated count that had already drifted, which is exactly the failure the map's no-number rule exists to prevent, so the guide now names the module and stops restating the size. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: that the prose is good. A checker cannot read a sentence; clarity is check_doc_style's measurable half (the map is inside its scope now) and the fresh-reader judgement stays with RC-17.

rows.name: naming-adr-implemented
rows.note: THE TYPE HALF OF THIS ROW IS NOW MECHANICAL (wave T15, 2026-08-21), and it was the half nothing could see. This note already said the namespace was trialled on autocomplete, TYPES and migration cost — but no analyzer was in the toolchain and no gate row typechecked, so the one property that made Facet.Controls worth building (nineteen entries with real spec types) was the one property no check could falsify. luau-lsp is pinned in rokit.toml and tools/check_types.py is narrow ON PURPOSE: it gates the diagnostics of TWO target files (src/init.luau and the witness) and ignores the ~245 pre-existing diagnostics in the require graph, because a lint regime over a tree nobody has type-cleaned is a different project and would make this row impossible to keep green. Two halves, neither sufficient alone: a positive witness hands each entry a local declared with the control module's OWN Spec (a wrong or narrowed parameter type reddens), and a GENERATED negative probe hands each entry a number (the fifteen typed ones must REJECT it, and the four that take any today are pinned by name so the set cannot grow). Three mutations bite under --selftest; the one that matters is an entry widened to any, which is exactly what a lazy-require refactor produces and what the suite, the surface dump and every other check in this row pass in silence. The public call-shape decision: Facet.Controls.Table-style role namespace trialled against one consistent flat alternative on representative screens, autocomplete, types, and migration cost; one ADR recorded; the chosen surface made coherent through the existing deprecation policy with Rascal Rally updated in the same change. IMPLEMENTED IN WAVE R5. The old two-argument composite form made an author write the library's name twice — the first argument was the library handing itself to its own builder — and nineteen composite controls shared a top level with eleven infrastructure constructors, so `Facet.` completed to forty-four mixed entries. Facet.Controls is one frozen table of nineteen typed entries, each closing over the library; every old form still works and is declared in the ledger at since=0.10.0 / removeNoEarlierThan=0.12.0 naming its exact replacement, which is the compatible half of the migration rather than a promise. 348 framework call sites and 18 doc samples moved; Rascal Rally moved 53 in the same wave (3 shipped client sites and 50 contract specs) even though the deprecation let it defer, because the drift guard scans that repository too and a consumer left on the retiring form is where the next author copies from. WHAT A TEST CAN PROVE HERE IS THE PART THAT MATTERS: an entry wired to the wrong builder — or to the right builder with the wrong library — still returns a perfectly plausible table, so all nineteen are built BOTH ways from one spec and compared on what they PUBLISH, and both mutations redden it. THE SAME DAY, THE OPPOSITE CALL: ADR-0038 renamed the public theme-authoring tags luau-*/luau-slot-* to facet-*/facet-slot-* OUTRIGHT, no alias — 395 occurrences across 56 files — because a call site lives in someone else's source while a selector lives in a theme package, and the complete set of theme packages in existence is the eleven in this repository. check_brand_drift could not SEE those tags (BRAND is luau[\s._-]?ui and there is no ui after luau in a tag), so 346 surviving old names were structurally invisible to the guard whose whole job is noticing one; it gained the family, case-sensitively, with five toolchain stems excluded and both halves selftested — a planted tag caught, a planted luau-analyze NOT caught, because a guard that cries wolf is a guard people route around. THE NAMESPACE COUNT IS DERIVED, NOT PINNED (2026-08-21, from the fresh-agent control exercise). The first half of that comparison used to be the literal nineteen, and that made this row CONTRADICT the playbook it is supposed to back: docs/extending/new-control.md §0 says never edit this file for a control, on the premise that the existing checks pick a control up — but a hard-pinned count is picked up by turning red, and the one-character fix was the one edit the playbook forbade. The row now compares the public surface's Controls count against the number of DISTINCT controls the conformance registry declares, so a properly registered twentieth control moves both sides and passes, while a namespace entry with no registry row (or a registry row with no namespace entry) still reddens. Measured four ways before it landed — unmutated PASS, entry-without-row FAIL, row-without-entry FAIL, both-moved PASS — and measured on the SHELL TEXT this row really produces rather than on a hand-retyped copy of it, which is what caught the first cut: the derivation was originally written with an escaped quote inside the command substitution, the formatter correctly normalised the escape away (the two spell the same character in a single-quoted Luau string), and the resulting NESTED double quotes collapsed the grep pattern to one that matched nothing. It counted zero and the row failed while a bash-quoted retype of the same idea passed. A run string in this file is shell source: keep every pattern in ONE level of plain double quotes, and prove a change by extracting the row and running it, never by retyping it. The deprecation count beside it stays the literal nineteen ON PURPOSE — a control born after 0.10.0 has no old form and no deprecation row, so that number is a fact about the migration set rather than about how big the namespace is.

rows.name: tile-game-crossword-loop
rows.note: TILE-1..TILE-12. The finite word-building loop: first turn crosses the highlighted centre cell; a turn places rack tiles in one contiguous row or column; later turns connect to a committed tile; Submit validates the whole line against the shared example dictionary, commits, scores and refills from a deterministic bag; Undo returns uncommitted tiles; every refusal names its exact problem and preserves recoverable state; a visible goal and bounded turn count produce win, loss, summary and restart. rows.name: match3-motion-public-surface
rows.note: M3-1..M3-6. No TweenService, frame loop, arbitrary task.wait, raw instance offset, or second animation system in the example. Reduced motion preserves ordering, feedback, final state and the game's rules while removing decorative travel, and does not substitute another busy effect. rows.name: wardrobe-retired
rows.note: WARD-1..WARD-3. Wardrobe is gone from the tutorial gallery, the showcase picker, the curated standalone manifest, the public example catalog, screenshots, publishable places and the player-facing build, and is not selected as a replacement for another example. The framework behaviours and tests it covered were inventoried FIRST and any useful Facet coverage preserved by smaller focused fixtures or another selected experience. It is still cited by the Step 11 reference-validation record, so if it stays it has moved out of the public examples surface into clearly owned test evidence with the reason written down; it is deleted when nothing still requires it. Historical proof does not keep a retired example presented as a current one. CLOSED 2026-08-30, AND THE ORDER WAS THE PLAN'S: the coverage inventory ran FIRST and is the evidence artifact (artifacts/example-games-and-standalones/wardrobe-inventory.md), one row per behaviour, each naming where its proof now lives. THE HEADLINE MEASUREMENT REFUTED THE DESIGN'S OWN LEAD CANDIDATE: `UI.Stage` was named as the behaviour Wardrobe might be the only example of, and it is not — examples/reference/p2_cartwheel/screens/plaza.luau mounts a Stage and tests/reference/cartwheel_spec.luau proves the same four things Wardrobe's pane did (live host, setLighting + setCamera recorded, an orbit that actually re-aims, reduced motion PARKING it, and the declared fallback plate when stageHost answers nil), beside a dedicated 22-case tests/stage.spec.luau. Category tabs filtering a collection (p4_foyer) and the purchase confirm/reject lifecycle (p1_glade commerce, p3_sipworks orders, p2_cartwheel commands) were likewise already redundant. Only ONE behaviour had no other owner — the undo/redo equip history that disables at both stack ends — and that is one of the reasons the fixture MOVED rather than being deleted. THE OTHER REASON IS THE GATE: reference-app-validation is closed and earned, and five of its rows cite Wardrobe (responsibility-ledger, proof-avatar-editor-loop, device-matrix, fixture-axes, plus swiftui-parity-round3/reference-apps-reproved), so the plan's own conditional fired. The app is now tests/fixtures/retired/p5_wardrobe with a README stating what it is, which earned rows require it, that it is NOT a current example, and the deletion condition (no gate row cites it). Every player-facing route is gone: the scenario file, its ORDER entry, the .rbxl place, and the place-builder entry. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: it does not claim the retired app is still SWEPT — it is deliberately out of the overflow/theme corpus (a retired surface has nobody to be clean for), and the four theme-ledger rows it produced were deleted in the same change with the reason in that file's header. It does not claim a device pass: the wardrobe-grids-phone matrix cell was PLANNED AND NEVER DRIVEN, so retiring it removed a plan rather than a proof, and its claim is pinned headlessly by the spec's own Picked-for-you block.

rows.name: sipworks-loop-complete
rows.note: SIP-1..SIP-5. The opening screen explains the tea-house loop in one sentence and shows a compact Today's order task with progress; the deterministic loop runs paid order to final stamp to free pour to an unmistakable completion state and a Serve another customer reset, seeded one stamp short so the lesson does not need ten repetitive orders; a rejection explains what happened and how to retry without losing progress; the catalogue, search, favourites, Blend Book, localisation, async states, compact-link entry and adaptive navigation stay useful secondary exploration that never buries the task; and player-facing proof jargon — 'reference proof', stage IDs, gate language, capability-ledger codes — is gone, with a short optional What this shows explanation after the play task rather than in place of it.

rows.name: glade-loop-complete
rows.note: GLADE-1..GLADE-5. The opening screen explains that wisps visit glades with fresh dew and suitable nectar and shows one deterministic Prepare this glade task for a named glade and its named wisp, with two plain progress rows and a clear first action; refilling the dew and choosing the preferred nectar makes the wisp visibly arrive or brighten, completes both rows and presents an unmistakable success state with Prepare again; a depleted or advanced condition explains itself and lets the player recover; and browsing, search, favourites, other glades, visitor history, flora, commerce fixtures and Keeper settings stay secondary and never become required to understand the loop.

rows.name: one-manifest-drives-places
rows.note: STAND-1..STAND-7. One checked-in manifest drives the showcase registry, the presentation-target and world-fixture metadata, standalone project generation, build outputs, documentation and drift tests — and no parallel list survives it. Today the seven tutorial names are spelled out independently in five files and the five reference proofs in six, and nothing cross-checks them; the themes build already derives its list and says so in its own header, which is the shape to copy. The seven tutorial places stay because the guide teaches them, five to seven curated existing showcase standalones plus the required world terminal ship, every required capability family is covered, and the reason each place was chosen — and each unchosen scenario left showcase-only — is recorded. Every declared place rebuilds and opens as a local self-contained .rbxl with no publish, upload, universe ID or Rojo requirement at play time, and the manifest reddens for an orphaned or missing output.

rows.name: places-are-playable-not-fixtures
rows.note: STAND-4. Each standalone shows a title, the player goal or task, a discoverable first action, visible success and failure feedback, reset, and a short optional What this shows explanation. Test-only jargon and raw counters are off the player surface unless the number IS the lesson. A standalone should feel like a small screen from a real game first and a diagnostic fixture second.

rows.name: shared-theme-and-motion-chrome
rows.note: THEME-1..THEME-5. Every tutorial and curated standalone place exposes the existing theme picker with the public reference themes actually mapped into the place — today the tutorial places mount the picker chip but their build maps no FacetThemes folder, so every one of them offers Studio Neutral and nothing else. A theme change updates palette, type, metrics and applicable chrome without remounting or losing game state. Every place with decorative or informational motion exposes the shared Full/Reduced control and writes the same reducedMotion environment fact as the showcase, reusing the showcase settings model and its chrome and reservation rules rather than copying them per place. The controls stay reachable without covering the example on small portrait, short landscape, ten-foot and Largest text, and their focus scope neither traps focus nor steals it from the example.

rows.name: dead-example-audit
rows.note: CLEAN-1..CLEAN-4. Every example source, generated place, project file, registry entry, test, guide link, build output and artifact reference is inventoried, and an old item is deleted only when it is superseded and nothing — tutorial, showcase, standalone, test, gate, document or build — still uses it. Stale generated .rbxl outputs, lock files, temporary projects and dead registry entries go. Known candidates already located: examples/table_phaseb/ has no project file and is referenced by no build script, examples/showcase.project.json is superseded by the heredoc project inside tools/build_places.sh, and a Facet-Showcase.rbxl.lock from a live Rojo session is sitting in the tree. Evidence whose provenance requires it is preserved outside the public branch rather than destroyed, and the audit ends with no unexplained item.

rows.name: rascalrally-consumer
rows.note: The consumer lockstep rule: Rascal Rally's normal and debug Rojo projects mount GameStudio/ui/Facet/src directly, so a Facet source, public-contract, default, behaviour, asset or distribution change is incomplete until its direct game consumer is synchronized in the same stage. This stage's framework change is the new render target; the game does not use it, so the honest deliverable is an audited consumer-impact ledger plus the game-side compatibility evidence proving the live consumer is current — not a manufactured edit. Game behaviour, content ownership, feature flags, the production Facet Sponsor default and the UseFacetSponsor = false legacy rollback are preserved.

rows.name: step-13-guards-hold
rows.note: Step 13's product-language and clear-writing guards, its comparison allowlist, and its brand-drift and call-shape drift checks still pass over everything this stage wrote — documentation and examples included. The release-candidate review already read this surface; nothing here is permitted to walk it back.

rows.name: prior-gates-unregressed
rows.note: The full tools/prior_gates.sh sweep regenerated at the judged source on a quiet machine, with every red either absent or allow-listed BY NAME with fresh justification rather than inherited. This row is also the stage's own headline measurement: the sweep is the dominant cost the optimization half exists to reduce, so its before and after numbers belong in the same artifact as its verdict.

rows.name: fresh-phase-gate-review
rows.note: GATE-3. An independent fresh-context phase-gate reviewer is given the goal, the acceptance ledger, the changed source and the raw artifacts — without the implementer's conclusions — plays the touched loops, and every requirement-affecting finding is fixed or explicitly dispositioned. Fresh context is the point: a verifier that shares the implementer's context shares its blind spots.

rows.name: suites-green-at-close
rows.note: GATE-1, GATE-2, GATE-4. Both suites serve green cached transcripts for the final tree, the affected prior gates rerun green, the representative Studio scenarios preserve their baselines, and every remaining physical or human row is named with one exact closing procedure. Earns a run string only when the close-out artifact exists.

rows.name: standalone-consumer-proof
rows.note: DR-12. examples/consumer/ mounts, themes, takes input, adapts layout, honors preferred text and tears down through public API only, with no Rascal Rally or parent-workspace import (check_boundary), from a fresh clone.

rows.name: package-metadata-and-manifest

rows.name: package-interface-refusals
rows.note: DR-14. tools/package.sh build/status/verify run offline by default; create/publish are dry-run without --confirm and refuse stale source, wrong asset id, wrong owner, dirty tree, missing secret, version/hash mismatch, red gates, in-flight operation and newer cloud revision — each refusal proven by a test before any network call.

rows.name: protected-manual-release
rows.note: DR-15. tools/release.sh checks out the exact commit, reruns the release tier, publishes only the configured asset id, polls, reads back and writes a receipt; it never publishes on ordinary commits or from forks; the workflow file mirrors the same guards.

rows.name: structured-results-replace-greps
rows.note: DR-16. The suite emits per-case structured results with stable ids; no gate row greps a transcript; a missing result id fails loudly (check_manifest_integrity retired or repointed).

rows.name: single-execution-per-identity
rows.note: DR-17. One release run executes each unique producer at most once per exact identity, measured from the invocation trace, including the Rascal Rally suite and each package/Studio canary.

rows.name: invalidation-rejects-bad-evidence
rows.note: DR-18. Stale identity, truncated or partial, failed, manually edited, wrong-toolchain and wrong-environment results are refused for reuse; perf/Studio/device/network classes are never upgraded by a headless cache — each proven by a mutation.

rows.name: tiers-and-explain
rows.note: DR-19. affected/fast/full/release exist; the run reports tier, producer selection reasons, reused results, invalidation reasons, slowest work and the smallest rerun command; affected/fast output cannot pass as full/release evidence.

rows.name: coverage-map-no-silent-loss
rows.note: DR-20. Every deleted or merged check maps requirement, failure direction, fixture and negative control to one surviving producer in the coverage map; no requirement in requirements.json is left without a current producer.

rows.name: mutation-parity-old-vs-new
rows.note: DR-21. A frozen corpus of at least twelve mutations reddens both the old manifest path and the new coordinator; recorded with commands and verdicts before the old path is archived.

rows.name: timings-and-budget
rows.note: DR-22. Cold and warm release-tier timings are recorded with percentage reduction; headless work is within twenty minutes on the documented machine or every irreducible producer is owned with class, cost and trigger; Studio/device/external time is reported separately.

rows.name: prior-gates-reevaluated-not-replayed
rows.note: DR-23. Every earlier phase's rows are evaluated from the same current run; prior_gates.sh replay is retired; a checked-in old PASS is never evidence.

rows.name: rascalrally-synchronized
rows.note: DR-24. The consumer-impact ledger exists; the Rascal Rally suite ran once at the final identity and is green; the game-side contract tests cover any Facet contract change from this stage (or record no-caller-change).

rows.name: public-tree-reproducible

rows.name: fresh-clone-works

rows.name: example-places-rebuild-from-clone
rows.note: DR-27. Every declared tutorial and curated standalone place rebuilds from the clone; the manifest, theme/motion controls, dictionary provenance, world-terminal fixture and generated-output policy survived cleanup; no retired output ships.

rows.name: package-from-clone-matches
rows.note: DR-28. The Package built from the clone matches the clone's source hash, the semantic manifest, the standalone consumer's tree, and (after the checkpoint) the private cloud copy.

rows.name: fresh-agent-builds-screen
rows.note: DR-29. A fresh agent given only the candidate repository builds a small adaptive, themed, stateful screen with public APIs; structural/instruction failures fixed.

rows.name: fresh-agent-extends-behavior
rows.note: DR-30. A fresh agent given only the candidate repository diagnoses or extends a bounded behavior through the documented workflow without private context.

rows.name: fresh-reviewer-chooses-from-guide
rows.note: DR-31. A fresh reviewer picks a library for several stated projects from the guide alone; fails if it needs private context, mistakes React Bindings, says Facet ships on Fusion, uses social-status comparisons, or treats inference as benchmark evidence.

rows.name: owner-packet-complete
rows.note: DR-32. The packet holds candidate commit/manifest/checksums/size, gate + license + provenance results, verification counts/timings/parity, audited remote state, the copyright line, repository settings to apply, the ordered rename/publish/rollback checklist, and the SwiftUI archive path/checksum + history decision.

rows.name: private-package-id-and-update-proof
rows.note: DR-33. After the owner checkpoint: one private Package asset with a recorded stable id/creator; inserted by id into a clean place it shows PackageLink, matching version/tree/hash, runtime mount/theme/input/update/teardown; a same-id update reaches an unmodified opted-in copy and a modified copy is reported, not overwritten.

rows.name: repository-renamed-and-verified
